Nana and I are discussing something quietly and looking at a magazine – whether for real or show I'm not sure – but I can't remember what. Either something on the show or something the girl said triggered it. It's about something we heard earlier and we don't want to talk about it in front of this girl, so I tell her to remind me later.

Tiff and I reconnect and are spending surprisingly peaceful and fun time in Gatlinburg. It is dark. There is a men's singing group (green costumes, reminds me of pipers) doing some kind of memorial by the street. It is the first time they have done it and I think it is going to be a regular occurrence.

I'm sent to Gallion to discuss a dnc, but she tells me she thinks I'm pregnant. "I think you're about to throw a person," she says. I decide to forgo the test. In case I'm pregnant, I would rather have the baby.

I am in the hospital with Nita and Angie at a nurses' station. Dr. Khan approaches us at the counter next to me and addresses me. He says I'm the one who asked him about gallstones. I say yes, suddenly aware of a dull discomfort in my right side. He says people have been telling him about me. All of us sit down. He says he has been told that I am well-off and not married, and he is interested in dating me. I am shocked anyone would say such and uncomfortable with the situation. He seems very flat and disinterested, in contrast with what he is saying. Nita and Angie listen but say nothing.

The setting is an impoverished country. There is a young boy who is supposed to grow up to be a great leader and deliver his people. But he is just a child. Two other young boys see him wake up one day, and suddenly he is a grown and strong man. They say it's a miracle. One of the boys says, like Jesus. I am dressed in a solid white bodysuit. I have a spiked white halo that surrounds my head like a sunburst. I am running with the man. We stop in a field. We are going to confront the evil that has kept these people under submission. (Note: Reading Dekker's 'Mortals' before I fell asleep.)

Joyce has a new slogan for her encouragement wellness group. I see it on a white toboggan trimmed in red with a picture of a glass of red wine. "Enjoy every day: a glass of wine, a good memory, a peaceful experience".

I am leaning over a table or short bed, possibly an exam room. I happen to glimpse my reflection in the mirror behind me and it appears I have lost weight. The old black jeans I am wearing fit very well and I think my butt looks cute in them.

Mom and I are at Desi's house. It is very neat and orderly. It is just as and the girls. Angelica is there with Tori. They are sitting side-by-side at the short end of the table working on a project. Mom is watching them. Tori is happy in saying something in laughter, and Angelica is silently making fun of her, which I ignore. As I leave the room I turn back to Mom and make a slapping gesture. I want something to eat, but everything Des has in a flat, slide-lid refrigerator is meat products. They are all in neat containers. One is a cylinder container of nothing but bacon. She has in her cupboards side items like rice boxes. With all this food she says she has nothing to eat and wants me to go out and get her something. I think this is very similar to when Will left and Mom and I helped her so much.

Mom and I are in a homeless community and it is nighttime. We are all sitting at long tables set up in the open streets, waiting for kind people to bring us something. A lady and her assistants are going through the crowd calling out names. They call my name and come to our table. They take something out of a large black plastic bag and set it before me for which I am thankful. Mom is beside me but I don't see her directly.

I am on the deck of a house that seems like ours in Versailles. I am caring for a golden and white guinea pig and two brown goats. The guinea pig is reclining comfortably in its cage as I am arranging the cage on a brick table. I noticed the cage has no lid, so the guinea pig is free. There is a large decorative thing like a big block made of various woodchips. It's supposed to go with the cage but I am unclear what to do with it; so I simply stand it up right beside the cage. A white goat comes and begins to talk to me. One of the brown goats approaches her aggressively and I say he is very protective over me. He gets right in her face and she stands her ground until he finally leave her alone with me.

In the middle of the night I hear Mom coming up the steps and try repeatedly to call out to her but find I cannot speak. Only breath comes out. She comes into my room and begins asking questions. I remain unable to talk. She does not seem to understand.

The front window of my car is cracking. There is a tingling sound as a barely visible crack spreads like a spiderweb. I am driving it, trying to get to a garage. I see two clear indentions in the metal frame above the windshield. I arrive at a garage but they see nothing wrong with it. I show them the indentions and that it is cracking. As I am trying to get them to look at it it shatters and all the glass falls into the car. (Rather similar to the actual incident in which the back window, with a tingling spiderweb, shattered into the car, and a service man said it had been hit twice with an object like a crowbar.)

Happy is visiting with me. We are standing in a white room lined with tables, similar to one of our seminary classrooms. In the course of our conversation he tries to kiss me, and it is awkward, it does not feel comfortable to me. Later, having not heard from him for a long time, I began to think about it. I talk to his mother (deceased in reality), and I am shocked to learn that he has died. I have just begun to reconcile that I have feelings for him and cannot believe he is gone.

Luke is directing a play at the hospital and I am in it. I cannot recall details, other than we are in a white room standing around long tables and working on the play. We all seem happy and work together well. Luke is standing in the center of the room, smiling.

I am sitting at a table in the Tackett's old house with Mr. Shep. The family is somewhere around but I don't know where. I feel very discouraged and Mr. Shep is encouraging me to persevere. I say it must be easier for him, living in Tennessee with less taxes. He asks if I think something is easy. I realize it is not.

I am walking up a street in town, going toward the end of Main Street. On the ground among brown fall leaves I see a bracelet made of tiny red beads. I think Tori would like it and I should pick it up for her. But I don't. Perhaps someone will come back for it. Several steps later, I see another bracelet, this one made of larger red beads. I pass it, staring down at it, considering turning to pick it up for her.

I am watching a recording of an experiment. Six guinea pigs have been put into one cage. Within a certain amount of time, one has died. They expect others will soon as well. I am angered and offended and turn off the recording.

I am sitting in the audience at a rehearsal, watching myself work on stage. I have auditioned for the local theatre. I am given a small role. I am frustrated, but then happy, thinking I can put all my focus into creating this supporting character and show them what I can do.
I get a text from Mom asking me where I had sent my Christmas wish list – to repair/clear three charts. I tell her I had texted it to her. I am suddenly hopeful that she will actually do it.

I am present for a rehearsal in which Stephen and a dark-haired girl are rehearsing and Italian scene. He goes to the bathroom but suddenly comes back out and kisses her. I am devastated. He goes back into the bathroom and closes the door, and she casually talks to me about something I don't even hear. I feel I can't even move. Later he and I are sitting at a table and I am aching to tell him that I still love him. I don't know how I can continue to associate with him like this. But just as I start to say something, another man appears at the table, then I second man. Stephen is talking to one and the other is talking to me. How will I ever tell him? I cannot go on like this.

I am moving into a college dorm temporarily for some reason. I'm walking through the hall with a friend and we see a pair of grey Eddie Bauer slacks hanging over a kind of platform at the front of a room. At the same time, she says, "your favorite pants!" and I say, "my favorite pants!" The girl from the room emerges from the platform and we explain that's my favorite place to shop. She is a new freshman. She asks if we're going there, and I say not yet but possibly tomorrow. She asks if we will come by and get her so she can go with us. I say sure. As we walk away, I wish I had gone to college as a normal girl.
I am in the office. The whole team is there. I have a horrible headache from my right temple. Jason is shocked that he can see a knot on the temple. He feels bad for me and tries to comfort me.

I am with two friends – one male, one female – in Gatlinburg. I am so glad that they have come to vacation with me. We are going down the main street looking for an Asian restaurant. They loved eating at a place called China King. On the left we see a new Chinese restaurant just preparing to open. The one they like is further down on the right and past that I think is Pekings. They ask what Mom likes to eat, and I tell them China King is also her favorite, that she eats there almost every day. We pass through a store filled with beautiful gemstones in natural and tumbled shapes. I am attracted to a large display of tumbled red stones that shimmer with blue reflections. They are called earthstones. I wonder what their properties are. I would like to get one.

I think I see two large black roaches in the foyer. There is still a lot of clutter. Mom has a vacuum cleaner there. I run to the kitchen. Still clutter here as well. I see another vacuum sitting on top of the counter. Several roaches, large and black, are running around the counter. I grab the vacuum and turn it on (I am surprised I can get it on – both vacuums are the one she keeps in the laundry room with the broken lever) but the narrow attachment at the end does not suck up the roach – it only bats it around the area. Then the roach lies and lands on the wall. I am trying to get the attachment off when several large black birds fly in the window and begin picking up the roaches and eating them, then flying out.

Mom and I are in the family room. It is still cluttered, but the floor is mostly cleared. I am able to sit on the carpet. She is sitting on a chair near me. I lift up the cushions on the couch and am surprised to find a wooden storage compartment underneath. It is empty except for tiny cloth dolls in vibrant single color simple dresses. It sparks a vague memory. I seem to remember sewing the dresses myself. Each doll is wrapped in an individual plastic bag, open at the top. I set them back down and consider the emptiness of the compartment. I ask Mom to help me start clearing some clutter and tell her we can use that space.

A large woman (reminds me of Alethea or Pam) is coming to work with us. She is trying to give me a foot massage. I offer to put socks back on, as I have had a bath but had my shoes on after that. She asks, Are they clean? I say yes. I don't think she actually ever does the foot massage. She is nervous she won't fit in. She reminds us she is Catholic and sometimes talks ghetto. I go to sit on a short sofa next to the desk where my coworker is. There is a huge window behind her, the storefront of our office/workspace, which is very large. The large woman comes and stands over me for a moment looking frustrated, then plops down beside me. The other girl and I try to encourage her.

We are in a multi bed setting like a large dorm room. Several people are there, including Diana, Mom, Tiff I think. Diana tells of someone we knew from Yellowstone who fantasized about shooting up elementary schools when he got drunk. He has come to her school today to talk to children. She tells me she brought a program to show me. Laughing, I jump out of bed and run to the kitchen to retrieve it. It has a cartoonish picture on the back of a man with long stringy blonde hair holding a rifle sitting on top of a tree. Diana, another girl and I moving into the apartment together. While the three of us are talking in the kitchen, I am looking for a food item and realize it is gone. I start thinking about paying for shared food and dividing the chores and cleaning.

Mom and I are in a new house. It is old but sturdy, well-built and sparsely furnished. Perfect. The door to my room is a heavy dark wood sliding door that does not fully close, but I don't mind. I am lying on the bed reading. Mom comes to my room to check on me. She knocks on the door, even though it is open it's usual couple inches, and I tell her to come on in, it's never closed. Two electricians come through, and I learn Mom has had them go through the entire house checking electrical outlets. They go into my bathroom to check a hidden space under the spa tub. There is a sliding door beneath where the former occupant hid something. They have the sliding door open when I come in. What I see behind the panel appears to be white lawn furniture. I don't know why it is there.

I am in Houston spending time with Stephen. We are now in a fine restaurant with rich woods and brass, dimly lit. We have spent a lot of time together and have talked late into the night. There are a few other people with us, but we seem very close. When everyone is starting to disperse, as it is very light, another man who has been with our group - and disturbingly reminds me of Stephen, thin with long, wild blonde hair - tells Stephen he is going to wait at a shop if he wants to join him and continue talking. I am concerned about this. The man leaves, then Stephen goes, I think to get his car, but he does not come back. One of the ladies who was with us says he has left. He did not even say goodbye to me.

Someone has given me a plate of meat-free "chicken nuggets". I take a bite of one and find it very undercooked. I don't want to offend the person who gave it to me, so I finish chewing the bite I took. I wonder if it will make me sick. But I am going to put the rest in the microwave until they are done.

I am in the yard at Nana Dadi's old house. Dad has come to take me to Lexington to have dinner with Granny Tackett. It is the first time I will see her new place. I am frustrated because Dad is backing a car Dadi has parked there for sale against the for sale sign close to the street, parallel to where my car is parked. I'm also frustrated that we are leaving so late, as it is 5 o'clock in the evening. I tell him I will barely be able to get there before turning around and traveling back in the middle of the night. We arrive at Granny's apartment. She seems happy. I go to hug her. As I do, I see behind her red bricks and dark wood, and it is like I am looking at a back corner of the family room in her old home. I think that she has made this little apartment like her home. I feel happy for her.

I am at the Town & Country shopping center. I meet a lady in the parking lot who says she is an energy worker. I tell her about our group. She says she has no one to work on her. I tell her about Cheryl, and suggest they trade sessions. I point to the beauty salon, although I cannot see the distinguishing animal prints or the name, and tell her Cheryl works there. She suddenly seems disinterested and says maybe she will call her later and leaves.

I am supposed to sing a solo in church. The time of the service has come, Brad and I have exchanged microphones and switched their batteries, and I prepare to saying. However, the song track starts in the middle of the song, so it is turned off. Kim goes up to see what is the problem. I think if the track fails she can play it on the piano. While they are working with the sound, I go down to the second pew and take out the sheet music to study it, suddenly unsure what lines I am supposed to sing. I become concerned. It is a praise song that sounds patriotic, like 'God bless the USA.' I don't know why I cannot remember the words or the music. They are still working on the sound. I confidently speak into the microphone that it is a good song and they will want to hear all of it.

Mom and I are in town, where the old library used to be, attempting to buy tickets for some new entertainment. I suddenly get a call that Nita is at the radio station and wants me there immediately – they are going to interview the palliative care team. First I have heard of it. And it is the evening, so I am frustrated they demand us with no earlier notification. I hear or see an ad for the current radio show; it does indeed say "meet the palliative care team." I am frustrated. I want to know if Mom and I can do what we are there to do before I have to be at the radio station.

I am walking through the first level of the parking garage at the hospital, eating a hot baked potato with butter. Jason is walking toward me with three nurses who have been smoking. One of them reminds me of Georgie. He has not been smoking, and they are all talking about using the patch. Jason asks if he can have a bite of my potato. I offered him the bowl, but not my spoon. He takes a couple pieces of the potato and eats them. I can tell from his expression he thinks something is missing. I say it needs salt.

I am in a livingroom-type environment at a location the hospital owns. I'm alone in the room, slowly pacing and writing notes about a patient. Luke comes in. He is slightly laughing but seems bothered by something. He tells me he wishes people would stop telling him they are praying for him. I ask why. He says if you continue to pray for the same thing and it never happens, you might as well quit bring about it. He does not specify, but I think he is referring to marriage and family. He turns to leave. He speaks to someone briefly outside of this room before leaving the building, and I can see him through the glass panel in the door. I have two immediate responses: that he is extremely attractive, and that I am concerned for him.

Jason tells me Nita has scheduled for all of us to be at the cancer center at 8:30 in the morning. I told him I scheduled a meeting with the staff and patient's family, and the patient is not coming until 10. He says Nita wants us all there early to discuss, and in case the patient arrives early. I tell him it is ridiculous to show up an an hour and a half early for a meeting. I am very angry.

I am in Houston, visiting the theatre. We are in a group session, and Stephen is sitting next to me, although he is not speaking to me. Someone rolls in an IV pole with a bag of fluids and places it next to me. This gets his attention and he asks me what it is. I explain that once a week I have to have an IV infusion. I had the option of being admitted into the hospital weekly, or learning to do it at home. I have been doing it myself. He instantly becomes protective and wants to help. He takes me home to a white, well lit apartment with a lounging chair next to a window with white sheers. It looks similar to my window and chaise from my old apartment but the lounging seat is white. He tries to make me comfortable and watches closely as I carefully insert the needle into my arm.

I am in a theatre group. There is a new group with us – visiting or interns. One of the young men is my age and I think he is attracted to me. We are sitting in the audience watching community people do a presentation. While we are talking to people in the row in front of us, he leans over next to me and slips his hand around my heel. I wonder why he doesn't hold my hand. One of the new members has brought a cat with them. I am holding the cat during the presentation, but it jumps down and runs towards the stage. We all call it, but it jumps onto the stage, and several go to retrieve it. I am laughing and truly feel happy.

I am visiting Houston and am in a restaurant with former ADPlayer friends, including Brenda. Brenda is sitting at the bar, cutting up a plate of spaghetti for an elderly man I am sitting with. Stephen is there. I'm told he was married to Lindsey, and they have recently divorced. He looks miserable. Although I am standing beside him for some time, neither of us speaks to the other. He keeps his head down and frequently rubs his face. I feel the same old sickness of longing to be with him but refusing to pursue him. As I take the plate from Brenda to return it to the elderly man, I say to Brenda, He certainly looks bad.

It is late at night and we hear 80s rock music blaring outside. I go to the peephole and see a red car parked right against the porch, squeezed in between Mom's car and the garage. I recognize it as Kelly's car, and the red truck parked across the driveway behind it as DJs. I tell Mom, and tell her they are going to upset the neighbors playing such loud music. I go to my car and slowly drive past the yard. I see Kelly, a child, and an older man who is not DJ running around the yard, apparently doing fast yardwork. They do not see me. I feel concerned and unprotected.

Nana, in her old kitchen. She is wearing the yellow rubber gloves she used to wear when she washed dishes. She is making popcorn in the old pot with the thin lid and flimsy ring handle at the stove. Such a comforting scene. I imagine the whole family is gathered in the living room and we will all have popcorn together.

I wake up during the night. I am in my bed facing the wall, but it looks like the ceiling with bumpy plaster. There is black scroll across it and at first I mistake it for scratchy handwriting. Then I realize it is mold. I am so stressed at seeing it but feel there is nothing I can do about it. I shut my eyes tight and try to rest.

I'm in a nurses' unit at the hospital and see Dad walking down the hall with a small bouquet of flowers in his hand. I call out to him and he comes in. I tell him I'm busy but he can sit and wait. He does. While waiting on me, he tells nurses he had a crush on me when I first started working there. I say he needs to clarify that he's my father. I tell him the flower company where he bought the flowers is in trouble because they blatantly mentioned their name in the new Dracula movie.

Daddy Ish is staying with us. There is a very nice and neat guestroom, but the rest of the house is the same, with many doors closing off rooms. I am to drive him to Lexington on Wednesday to drop him off at Dad's house so he can take him to his assisted living apartment. I don't know why Dad insists on the middle of the week, as I have to work and will not get back till late, or why I can't drop him off at his apartment myself. He seems very depressed, and I am worried about him.

I am in a small room in the hospital with three doctors. The last one who comes in is supposed to examine the second one. She takes out her stethoscope and as she reaches around the second doctor's arm, she looks at me and mouths, Who is this? Still laughing with them, I look at the second doctor's name tag, but I can't remember the name. I go down the hall into an office alone. I am looking up Angie's phrase "who dat" on the computer. Suddenly I have a frightening feeling. The clock in the room is very loud and the ticking suddenly unnerves me. I realize I am in an office in Houston at St. Street.

The palliative care team is in Nita's car. We are driving on a country road somewhere beyond Cedar Creek. She says she is looking for an apple orchard. I think she is going to try and convince us all we have to go to the cancer banquet again. We go down a steep hill–a valley filled with water. It's like driving down into a swimming pool. The incline is steep, filled with water to the main road level. We plunge into the water and the car submerges as she continues to drive down. Little splashes leak in the top of the window glasses and I feel frightened. But as we go further no more comes in. I wonder how long we will be underwater before we reach the incline.

I am taking care of a mentally challenged man. We are going up concrete steps into a concrete building. It is a large indoor pool. He goes to the men's room, and after making sure he is safely inside, I go to the ladies'. As I walk along the path to the bathroom, I notice water running around my feet. Water is running along all the paths around the pool. It feels pleasant, walking in the water. It makes me want to go in the pool. I get to the ladies' room, and there are no toilets, just plastic yellow containers with small holes cut in the top of them. It is very awkward, but I squat and manage to pee in one. It feels very dirty in the bathroom and I can't wait to get out of there.

Des and I are at our old house. Mom is away, and Granny Tackett has come to help us. The house is very cluttered and covered with dust and cobwebs. I am concerned about having her there, but she doesn't say anything about the condition of the house. Des and I are sitting on the dirty orange carpet in the basement and she he is helping us feed dogs.

I am running along the street and Sox, Scout and Nyla are with me. I suddenly realize they are not on leashes, but they are running right along with me, staying in yards. I run back to the house to get them to follow. I open the garage door. The garage is completely cleared out, but the floor is dirty and there are a couple boxes stacked. Scout and Sox run in, and Scout immediately goes to a dirty place on the floor and lies in it. I go to her to pick her up, and she turns into a small white cat. I open the door to the house, and there is a wall of stuff blocking the path. I call for Mom but she does not answer. I hold Scout at the top of the wall and encourage her to jump down on the other side.

I am going to a movie alone. It is a production of 'a discovery of witches,' but it is not very good. The lead man is not at all attractive, and the story plot is really mixed up. In the scene I remember, Matthew is lying in a hospital bed holding a dark-skinned toddler with red eyes, and Diana walks in and he reaches to her and invites her to come meet their child. Later she is telling her aunt that she has married and had a child with a vampire. The movie seems to end and restart so many times toward the end I'm not really sure it's over, but I'm tired of waiting for the credits so I leave. In the theater hallway I run into a girl I know who played the lead role and she asks me what I think of it. I tell her it wasn't very well done and ask her if they are going to do a sequel.

I am in Pikeville on a Thursday. I am to play the lead in a show opening in Lexington on Friday evening. I do not know my lines. I'm not even sure if I have the most updated script. I think I will be cramming lines in the van all the way there and hope the people riding with me won't mind. I am nervous but a little thrilled at the aspect of opening a show.

I am driving Mom's car through a parking, lot looking for my car. I think I am driving a little fast and reckless to be in a parking lot. I see a police vehicle parked in the lot and think I should slow down. I drive the length of the lot, expecting to see the blue tip of my car, but do not see it. I spin around at the end and prepare to do another sweep, when I realize I'm driving Mom's car, so why am I looking for mine. I'm not towing it. I realize my car is not there, that I have been in her's all along.

I tell Mom I want to cut my hair but I can't seem to do it myself. I tell her I want it all cut off, like a burr cut. I hand her the scissors and wait anxiously as she begins to cut. When she finishes, I look in the mirror and see she has not cut it all off; she has left several inches of hair, especially around the top, and she has placed a hairband on it to secure it. The hairdo is straight and poofy. It looks pretty, but I am saddened by the sight of my beautiful long hair gone, even though I wanted it shorter. I think how I would have never cut my hair except that time Mom tricked me into it. I wonder at the irony of it now. I hand her the scissors and tell her no, to cut the rest of it off. I wonder if it is because I have cancer.

The palliative care team and I are in an apartment – or it could be a house, but it feel small. Jason is in the bathroom on the toilet and I am standing outside; we are apparently arguing. He says I am bipolar and should be medicated. I say maybe I am manic depressant and really like my manics. Then we are all out in the apartment sitting area. I am lounging on a sofa with a small gray and white cat in my lap. I start to pick up the thin cat and it yowls at me so I set it down. The second cat, tan and white, very friendly, climbs onto my chest. (No doubt this is from conversation with Granny regarding Dad's two cats and there polar opposite personalities.)

I'm with Penny and some theatre friends of hers. I ask them if they can make a living based on their theatre work. They say none of them makes a living on it, they do it because they love it. I am thinking of leaving the hospital and pursuing theatre full-time. I suddenly think I can remain in my work at the hospital and do theatre in the evenings.

Mom, Des and I sit with Aunt Froni at a picnic table in a clearing surrounded by mountains in front of a large house where the Wagner's are hosting a family dinner. For some reason she doesn't want to go in to eat. She is smiling but seems shy or uncomfortable. I offer to go in and make her a plate and encourage her to eat. She sheepishly excepts. I go through the large house to the area where all the food has been displayed and start making a plate for her. I smile and speak kindly to those around me, though I feel irritated with the Wagner's for inviting some and not others.

I am in Gatlinburg, walking the dogs in the neighborhood around the cabin. I see a car parked in front of the house for sale next to us, and Steve & Judy get out and walk toward me. I am surprised that they are the ones who have purchased the house. They say they have been talking about buying a house here for some time and just decided to do it. I am a little jealous. But very happy to see them.

I am visiting some old friends from seminary and they begin to play a video. Apparently it had been taken some time ago and they thought it might be fun to watch. In the video, I have just left a party at Tiff's apartment, and she and several of her friends have stayed behind. They are making this video apparently making fun of me. They are dancing and waving ridiculously, and Tiff, with a very strange expression – blank face, alert eyes, creepy smile – walks to the camera and begins sprinkling salt on it, as if she is sprinkling salt on me. I am very disturbed and insulted by this.

I'm getting off the elevator at the hospital and Roger and Rachel are there, waiting to get on. When they recognize me they don't speak, but hurry onto the elevator and leave. I feel very rejected and offended. But as I walk down the hall , several doctors – I specifically recall Dr. Youcif, and I think Alicia – extend a hand to me with a smile and welcome me to the floor. I realize God has placed me where I am appreciated. Ironically, when I woke up, I discovered Roger had been honored at an awards ceremony the night before, which Rachel had attended with her pseudo family – Catherine's in-laws – and we knew nothing about it. Typical.

I am in Gatlinburg. I go alone to a café run by gypsies. I feel uncomfortable as soon as I walk in. It is dark, and as I pass the bar in the main room, some gypsy ladies are sitting at a table opposite laughing at me. I am offered a place in a back room. An open curtain divides this room from the passage leading to the back. I feel very hesitant about going, but start to anyway.

Carrie or Penny have written a Christian book that is being published and promoted. I say Carrie or Penny because Carrie is on a Christian radio show promoting the book; I hear it come on and tell mom she is on the radio program. Julie tells me someone asked Des about her, and she informed them that she was my friend, not hers. However, when I see a copy of the book, I see Penny's name on it.

I am with Tiff in an elaborate mall-type setting. There is a lot of glass and metal, elaborate decor around us. She is expressing anger because Larry Penix's church has offered to pay for him to take a karate class. She said she wanted to take a karate class and they never offered to pay for hers and she could not afford it. I didn't know she even went to Larry's church. To make extra money she has been filming a video/commercial. She shows me a clip of it. She looks very pretty and happy. I wonder how she's having so much financial difficulty.

I am with Zack. There is a group of young men encouraging him to draw some graffiti. At first he agrees to join them, then backs out at the last minute. I received a letter from him back in my hotel room in which he states the first rule of some martial art is to refrain from something, and he believes this graffiti would fall into that category. I did not like the young men and I'm glad he has not gone with them.

I am in a theatre, sitting in the front row. There is a readthrough going on, and Kim is directing. I feel thrilled to be part of the readthrough. When we are done, I return the script to her and remind her if she any positions open to please remember me. I see myself trying on a Phantom of the Opera mask.

I am in a large lounge area connected with the hospital. Several executives are there. They tell me I am fired, but do not give me a reason. I come in the next day, to the same lounge area, and go through a food line to get a meal. I wonder if someone will tell me today the reason I have been fired. Nita is on her way back. Just before she enters the office, Jason comes in and tells me he has already told her that I was fired. (Working out extreme frustration over the apparent senseless firing of a rare qualified and ethical leader.)

I am sitting in the back of a steakhouse with Mom. Suddenly there is a rancid cigarette smell, and I turn to see a lady at the table next to us and her friend who has just arrived, both fat and both smoking. I turn to them and ask them to please put their cigarettes out. The lady who has just arrived scoffs, "Why can't I smoke? It's a public place." I go to tell a waitress and she follows me back to the table. The lady who had just arrived is now leaving, and the lady at the table is putting her cigarette out in her drink. The waitress politely tells her it is a smoke-free facility.

I am having sex with Arthur in 308. At least we are trying to: nothing is happening and I feel completely empty and unsatisfied. There is a song playing overhead with lyrics: this will not be our usual; this will only happen when I get the feeling. How horrible, I think. And yet I think that is exactly what we are doing. I think his wife, whom I've never met or seen. He kisses me deeply once. I want out of this as much as I want to do it.

I am walking down a hallway in the hospital. The walls surrounding me are white and the light is bright. I am limping badly and my hips hurt. My right leg has become longer than the other. I cannot walk fast. Even trying to walk at a normal pace is painful. I am pushing as hard as I can to reach the corner. I cannot go any faster.

Another 'Hell on Wheels' dream. I am married to Collin. There is a female mayor in the town. And there is a woman interviewing us. He introduces me as his wife, then points to his gun hanging on a rack beside me and says that's my son. Then he indicates the small boy in our home by name. I lean into him and say, "You realize you just introduced your gun as your son." When they are finished with the interview he seems tense. I lay my hand on his chest and ask him what is wrong. He says in all the years he's investigated murders he's never received false information. I understand. There has been a mass murder. I see in my mind several bodies in the river, as if I am looking up at them from the riverbed as they float in the blue water played with light. The person he is investigating lied to him.

Nita has written a description about me, sort of like a reference. I am reading it at my desk. She has described me as someone who swindles money from others. I am shocked and have no idea why she would say this.

Several people, including myself, are sitting in the ditch in front of the hospital facing the mountain. I think there is a waterfall or at least a trickling of water coming down the mountain in front of us. There is a very peaceful feeling about it. Suddenly there is an explosion of air in the middle of the group, blowing several people forward. I am on the very end towards the road. Those of us on the outskirts brace ourselves for the aftershock. It comes – a burst of air pushing me forward against the mountain. It is breathtaking and delightful. There is a woman standing behind me on the pavement – I think perhaps Tiffany or a representation of her. I am trying to explain to her how wonderful the experience is, but she is negating it and has no interest.

I am lounging on wooden stairs in a fairytale-like location. There are two huge houses made of wood, one on either side of the long flight of stairs on which we sit. Near us is a patio with a huge tree. Nita is sitting next to me, and Jason tells me to look at the bird in the tree. I look into the branches and high up in the center I see a wonderful birdhouse like a beautiful old-fashioned birdcage. There are three birds, one large one that is very beautiful at the top of the birdhouse. The scene is so lovely I am near tears. I lay my head on one of the wooden steps and tell Nita I so want to live in this house.

The palliative care team is living together in an apartment – Nita, myself, Jason, and a young African-American man about Jason's age. We live like a family and all get along well. We are very close. I remember cuddling with the young black man at one point. Someone comes to the door – I think to make a delivery – and as Nita is busy with it the delivery person tell me how much she admires and appreciates Nita. She explains to me that Nita has just donated $1600 – to a patient or a cause, I'm not sure. But it has something to do with a patient who could not afford something they needed.

I am sitting in a parking lot with Maurice and Kevin. They are sitting in the cab of a white tractor-trailer, and I am sitting on the ground beside the open passenger door. We are talking about family genealogy. I have two orders of chicken livers – I was supposed to be giving them to someone – and as we talk I begin to eat them. I suddenly can't stop and eat all of them. This shocks me. Later, I am at a picnic table with Mom. We are talking and I take a bite of a double cheeseburger from Wendy's. The next thing I know, I have eaten all of it and there are only fries left on the plate. Then I remember earlier in the day I ate a double cheeseburger from McDonald's as well. That's three times I ate meat in the same day. And I am a vegetarian.

It is dusk and I have just finished a murder landmark tour in a nearby city – I think it is Lexington. The tour has ended in a sort of park with grassy slopes and trees. As the others in the tour disperse, I stop to talk to a man who is also from Pikeville. He is helping to clean up and seems very excited. He is a large man – tall and wide with a bur cut and wearing a brownish jacket like a police officer's. I know as well as historical murder sites he is also into ghost hunting. I tell him maybe this is something we should bring to Pikeville. He says he absolutely thinks.

I am at a reunion in a sort of convention center. The reunion is for theatre people I worked with in college. I am standing in the lobby with a small group of former theatre friends from Morehead. Tiffany is talking about Danny Stockton – his Facebook page saying 'absolute Danny Stockton.' I have no idea what she's talking about and no interest. She seems very obnoxious to me. I look through the door into the main room and see Eddie. He is standing in front of a chair on the aisle right in front of the door. He's wearing a black suit. He looks older, handsome, although when he turns to me his teeth look unhealthy. His eyes are dark and when he sees me he appears angry. I rush to him to hug him.

I'm having lunch with Stephen, and it is very painful. He asked me out, but it is clearly only for selfish reasons; he only wants to talk about himself and has no interest in me. I have that same old feeling – an aching desire to be with him, and the painful realization he does not care for me in the same way. As he complains to me, I am thinking this is the last time I will go out with him. I do not deserve to suffer like this anymore. I don't want to get back into it, and I will not do this again. Later, I am traveling – walking or driving, unsure – on Hibbard Street downtown. There is a tiny hole in a pale yellow painted concrete wall next to me separating the streets. Out of the hole comes ladybugs, first just a few then a countless number – a cloud of ladybugs flying over me. It is interesting and somewhat delightful. I wonder what ladybugs represent.

Nita and I were at the meeting with Vergi's family we had scheduled for this morning. We met them in a greenhouse. Clifford was acting very strange. He kept walking around taking long steps and then suddenly bending over. I wondered if he was high. Vergi seemed agitated, and kept going back-and-forth. At one point she was making fairly clear decisions, then she accused us of talking about her behind her back, asking how we knew she had cancer in the first place. I told her she told me herself this past winter. She said she did not tell me. He seemed glad when she became aggressive with us, and then they left together. I must have really been concerned about the meeting this morning.

I am in a small, hard-working Western community (probably from watching 'Hell on Wheels' last night). A young man has fallen sick, and they have put his workload on myself and another girl. We are concerned that it is too much work for us to complete. I think the man needs a powder insulin shot, and that he is a day late because it is already Monday. I open my eyes and look out the window into the early light. I realize it is Sunday morning, and I'm grateful is not Monday. Then I realize Mom is supposed to take the powder insulin shot. I was worried she was a day late, but she has not missed it. I think to myself I must remember to remind her later today.

I went to work and was surprised to find there were now six of us in palliative care, and they had given us two additional offices – the two empty ones next two ours. We had all three open, and we seemed to have so much space our stuff look small. We kept the doors open and went back and forth working together.

It is dark and I am in Tennessee on a type of vehicle – a large black tour bus. Gatlinburg has become a dark and low place. Everything is black – buildings, streets. Some shops are lit but few people are on the streets at all. I see a homeless man sleeping on the street and comment to the driver I have never seen that before in Gatlinburg. A man driving a another tour bus suddenly backs into us. He looks back and sees us, says something rude, and immediately pulls away. We follow him to the tour station. There are mostly horse-drawn carriages there and a few buses. All the horses are large and black, like Friesians. We speak to a man there and explain to him that one of their tour guides backed into us and pulled away. I am so surprised at how dark and dangerous the town has become.

I see a house as if from the outside but I can see in the windows. The house belongs to Tiffany's grandmother. No one else is there with her. She has photographs of family covering the walls from top to bottom. The house is clean and bright. I think it is sad but also good for her to have her own house. There is something about Tiffany, her mother, and Linda, but I cannot remember the details.

I am with Mom and Luke and a friend of his. It seems we are in a large vehicle with space enough to sit facing each other. They are talking about someone who had to have their dog put down. Mom says she doesn't want to hear about it. There is something about a storm – a hurricane or tornado – and I am in another location. I think I am in Tennessee. I have helped the people I was supposed to help – it seems I have been doing some duty for the community with ADPlayers – and am calling Mom to let her know everything is okay and I will be home as soon as I can.

I am holding a family meeting at the hospital. We are in a space outside curtained rooms. The lighting is dim. We are sitting in a circle on hard chairs. One of the ladies talking to me is the patient's granddaughter, and I recognize her as a former employee. I believe she left due to drugs. I also remember her mother. I become very leery about the meeting. I ask Nita later if she remembers the mother and daughter. They have been in a family meeting before. The daughter's name is Gina, and I think the mother's name is Esther.

Pam posts on Facebook a picture of her family in a spacious closet complaining about how small it is. I comment to myself that the closet space she's complaining about is almost as much room as I have to live in. I am walking through a neighborhood that reminds me of Lake Joanne (Aunt Connie's old neighborhood). It begins to climb into a steep hill and I run up it. The wind is blowing up here; it smells sweet and for the moment that gives me joy. There are two blue houses I can see from the crest – one lighter blue and one newly painted darker blue. I pause to look at them. They are both huge homes. Marsha is there and someone else of Mom's friends. They ask if that is my house – the darker blue one I am looking at. I say no; the lighter blue one is Nana's (?) house, and that one is Rachel's.

I see Scout run onto the deck with a black snake in her mouth. It is small, I assume a baby. She is shaking it vigorously and I go out to get her to drop it. She finally does and I think it falls under the deck. I grab her and bring her inside. Then the unfinished hot tub is half-in-half-out of the kitchen wall. There is a lot of debris at the bottom of it, and I see the snake go under it on the kitchen floor. The snake has come into the house. There is an arrow, like a cursor, showing me where it is. I secure Scout in her crate to begin looking for it, frantic to tell Mom there is a snake in the house.

There is a reunion for my class at the high school. I have not had any interest in going. But suddenly on the day of the reunion I long to reconnect with those I went to school with. I rush to the high school hoping I am not late.

I am talking on the phone to Patty and tell her how much I miss everyone in Houston. When we hang up, I wish I could meet with them. Suddenly I am in a huge greenhouse. Marty and Kristi are there, and I think Tigger is with them. Kevin and Jen come in, and I am happy to see them. I think their dogs are with them too. I tell everyone I should go get my dogs so we can all play together.

The dream occurred in present time. I am jarred out of sleep by the front door being forced open against the bar and Mom screaming my name and shouting why didn't I answer my phone. My heart is racing and I feel terrified, being jolted awake like that. She wasn't supposed to be home until this afternoon. I distinctly recall checking my phone last night and making sure it was on. It has not rung. As I am getting dressed, I look out the window and see Mom sitting on the outside of the back fence with at least one of the dogs. She was not able to get in the front door so she went around to the back. I go out to let her in, and we sit on opposite sides of the hammock. My heart is still racing and I feel sick from the fear. I asked her why she would scare me awake like that.

I am at Des's dentist office. I am sitting in the empty waiting room, and Shonda is sitting at a desk with paperwork across the room from me. No one else is present. The room is very white. Shonda is telling me that she cannot provide insurance because she is just out of school, and will have to charge patients extra 4 years. I say that makes sense and she should add a $10 fee for every patient until she can provide insurance.

I am on an elevator in the hospital with several people including the palliative care team and Roy. Roy is happily talking about having feelings for one another. I hug him and tell him it is impossible. He silently holds me a very long time and seems sad. I assume he and Diana are together. Suddenly I'm not sure. I want to ask the others their opinion of his reaction, but don't. I wonder later if I have feelings for him, and I am determined to ask him.

I am at Granny Tackett's house. Her dog is standing in front of me looking at me and I am petting him. We are talking about the best place for him to have a new home. She says someone suggested she let him stay with the property. I just want him to have a good home with reliable people.

I am at the aunts' house in Louisa. There is a young girl there who calls both Marie and Audrey her grandmothers. She is asking if she can go to Maxine's house as she is bored here. I am amused and ask why she calls both of them grandmothers. Someone - an elderly lady I believe is a relative - explains to me that the girl's father was abusive, and Audrey and Marie killed him and hid the identity of the girl's parents. Therefore she does not know if Audrey or Marie is your grandmother so she calls them both grandmother. I am completely disturbed that this has happened and that everyone talks about it so casually.

I am driving on a road above Pikeville. It is nighttime and I see the lights of town below. I believe it is the road around the University hill, but in my mind I think it is called Harold's Street. When I reach the bottom of the hill, there is a long straight road ahead of me that crosses an intersection. I drive straight ahead in the dark, and find myself in a neighborhood in Houston, just a block over from our St. Street theatre office. I wonder if I drop by if I might catch Stephen rehearsing for something. I turn to head back to the main road, only glancing toward the theatre building in passing. I drive on, and I find myself in daylight in Gatlinburg, meeting Mom, Des, and the girls for a girls' only vacation at the cabin. Mom asks where I've been and what took me so long.

I am working in a theatre here in town. During intermission, I am talking to someone in the lobby and I see Tiffany's mother and sister. I do not speak to them and they passed by. I think it odd that they are at the theatre. I know that Tiffany is dead, and I think about this when I see them. I don't really feel any particular way about it.

I am standing on something for height reaching through the fence to trim a tree that is growing through from Rhoda's side. It has thin leafy branches and pink flowers. I say I am glad it is in their yard. I seem happy about the work.

Nita and I are doing a case study. The man looks like Robert De Niro. He is 88 years old, and he meditates every day with a hologram machine, causing his hologram to do extreme yoga strengthening for long periods. He and his hologram are amazingly built for his advanced age and appear to be younger due to muscle, posture, and strength.

Mom and I are on the top floor of a parking garage. There is a cream standard poodle dog that I know, and she runs toward us to play as soon as she sees us. Her coat feels damp but I scratch her ears anyway. I tell Mom about all the animals that live there.

I am touring a new house Mom has purchased and renovated. There is an older man there – I am not sure who he is. The part of the home Mom is living in has been nicely done. I am surprised to find that attached to the home is a huge section that has not yet been finished. It is almost barn-like in its rustic wood, yet appears it was once a grand room with high vaulted ceiling. I am eager to find out what she will do with the rest of the house.

I come downstairs, and Mom shows me a cleared and clean space in the family room. It still looks a little cramped because the clearing is so small, but it contains a sectional sofa and chair around the television. I am so excited, and tell Mom how thrilled I am with what she has done. Later two friends come to the driveway to meet me – a man and a woman. I let the man into the house and show him the new space. I express how grateful I am that I can now sit and watch tv with Mom. He doesn't seem overly thrilled and looks at the kitchen then goes back out. I notice that the kitchen is still cluttered and the living room is full to the doorway. I don't care. It is a start.

I am talking to a family who is making a homemade racing car – the old fashion long and pointed wooden kind. I'm trying to have a serious conversation – I think it is about a palliative care patient who is their father. I'm not sure if they're listening, they are so intent on making this car. Then I am in a place like a school playground, except all the students appear to be adults. I see a lone young man in knee-length jean shorts and a gray t-shirt sitting on a concrete structure. He looks rather withdrawn and sad, but I know he is going to be the one to race the car – and he is perfect for it. I also see in the crowd Kiefer Sutherland and think he is going to be in the race as well. There is something about a teacher there, but I cannot remember what.

I meet a new family coming to town – a man and his wife and their two children. He is going to be a new pastor in the area. I am rooming with Penny in a small house. The family has asked me to housesit for them, and I need to pick up some personal items first. I don't want to wake Penny for some reason. I don't want her to know that I'm going. I quietly go into the house, get what I need, and slip back out. Just as I'm getting in the car and starting to back away, the lights come on. I hurry out of the driveway and head toward the house where I am housesitting. It is a huge home with lots of glass and at least one pet – a friendly dog. I love it there, but when it is nighttime it is very dark and I feel rather exposed because of all the glass. Still, it is very beautiful and I enjoy being there.

I'm shopping in Kmart and go to the dressing room. A lady dies in the stall across from me. I leave, assuming the staff is calling the authorities. A week or two later, I return to the store with a friend and we go to the dressing room. I think I glimpse the body, still slumped in the same dressing stall. I can't believe it is still there. Suddenly my friend points it out. The body looks old, a dirty orange look. We go to the staff, and they ask us not to tell anyone because they are renovating and don't want to get bad reviews. I notice that several things around the staff area have been cleaned up and are bright and white. I am stunned they have left the body in the dressing room and wonder what they're going to do with it. I wonder if there's someone I can anonymously call to report it.

I'm standing in a field and many animals are around me. I saw them all clearly in the dream but now only specifically recall a deer, a peacock, and the one that came nearest me was a buffalo. I was literally surrounded by a variety of animals from God's kingdom. I felt a wonderful sensation of purpose and belonging. I felt someone approaching me, and when I turned I saw it was the Buffalo, coming very close to my left side. He was almost right against me when he stopped and began to paw the ground. I remember thinking I wasn't supposed to touch one, but he was so close. As I turned to leave the field the Buffalo followed me. So naturally, I put my arm around him and rubbed his shaggy mane. As I walked towards the street where other people would be, I told him that he would have to go elsewhere eventually. A man came toward our direction on the street, and the Buffalo separated from me and went another way.

I am talking to four people, including one interracial couple (a black man and white woman) who work with Penny at some job. They all wear odd paper hats and have to keep their hair very short or up under the hats. I am talking to the four outside of the little shop and Penny is in the window of the shop closing up. She turns out the lights and begins to close the shades and shouts good night to everyone then turns and leaves. I wonder why she is sleeping in the shop. I think the white lady who is dating the black man is going to be my roommate tonight and I shall ask her about their new job.

I am at the hospital and Tori is with me. She wants me to take her to the roof. I don't know why she wants to go but I agree. We get into an elevator and ride all the way up to the roof of the hospital. I have a little room there – not like an office, but like a studio apartment – with a small bed neatly made with a red bedspread. Tori goes to the edge of the roof, and I warn her not to go any further. She sits down just a few feet away from the edge and looks at the view in silence.

I am dating Michael Hall. Actually, I am very much in love with him. We are at some event at a dirt track. He tells me he has received word that the Dexter show may be starting up again. He is very excited about it. I am too, but am concerned about his acting in sex scenes. Later, at the event, he is facing the dirt track and I am facing him. My arms are around his waist and his arms are around me. My face is pressed against his coat – a heavy gray coat – and I notice the smell is not pleasant. I wonder where it has been. I wonder if he loves me as much as I love him.

Today's nap. I am in the hospital. I have heard that Stephen is coming to visit someone. I know he's going to the fifth floor, but I don't know when. I'm standing at the elevator, hoping I can go to five and see him. Then, for some reason, I am on the floor behind an object, like a cart, and can only see the elevator indicators and the bottom of the door. The indicator lights up - it is going to five - and it also says his name on it, along with the number. I look inside the open door and see his shoes. I try to reach under the object and hold the door open, but I don't have enough leverage and it closes.

I am going out with Jeff. I don't think we are seriously dating, but we are having a date. He runs into a woman he met before, and she tells him she is pregnant. Apparently they only went out once. He tells me that he's not sure what's going on, but she may be pregnant with his unborn child. He goes to another room in the place we are – a bar, restaurant, and shopping center are connected. While browsing random wares, I happen to look out a window and see him getting on a motorcycle, and a woman who appears to be drunk is getting on behind him. They drive away. I am so confused. Later I am talking to a mutual friend who had previously asked him if he liked the girl he had gone out with before, and she is surprised to hear the girl is pregnant.

I was standing at the road in front of the high school and there was a tree there. The tree was V-shaped with a low fork. Dr. Bartley was leaning in the fork of the tree, holding onto the branches. I think he was helping some children there. We talked for a little while and then I left. Later I was at the farm, again near the road. The same tree was there, and Dr. Bartley was leaning on it the same way. We were talking and I think he was feeding animals across the fence. A little while later I was near the street again and saw him go into a bakery, to get food for a needy family, I thought. When I looked again he leaning in the fork of the same tree the third time. I commented that I kept seeing him in the tree.

I am sitting on a bed and an elderly lady's apartment, dressed in a satin robe. J, through Tiff, is attempting to seduce me. I am not giving into him. I see the old lady come into her living room. There are no walls, only open space between the bedroom and the living room. I get up and go to her bathroom. When I come out, he is sitting on the sofa next to the old lady. They appear to be watching TV. He looks at me, and his eyes are evil and he is smiling. His expression strikes terror in me. The old lady's head is hanging down, her chin on her chest, and I know he has killed her. I am disgusted and horrified and just want to leave the apartment.

I am on a beachy area. The tide has just gone out and the sand is still very wet - that wonderfully saturated sand that makes you feel like you're walking on a bubble. Walking along, I see a grey fish lying on its side in the wet sand, surrounded by a shallow puddle of water. It is clearly struggling to breathe. I pace the beach looking for a stick with a soft enough end to lift it up and move it towards the water. I finally find an appropriate stick. I gently lift the fish and put it in the water.

Nita and I have been called to another facility. I think it is the cancer center, but it is up on a hill. We are at the top of a steep concrete driveway. Someone gives us a strange dark red/maroon motorcycle with two seats to ride back to the main hospital. Nita gets on the main seat and begins to put on her matching helmet. I start to sit on the side seat – sort of a little wire basket off the side of the main seat. She stops and asks me if I have had training in the proper use of wearing a helmet. Holding the second matching helmet, I tell her I know how to wear it, but the only training I've had in that was when I got a scooter as a girl. She excepts this and we prepare to ride back to the hospital.

Mom and I got into a horrible discussion over the house. We are sitting across from each other at an empty table – not here. She is indicating she has no intention of clearing, after years of promising to do so. In anger and anguish, I tell her how badly it is affecting me – anxiety attacks, unable to sleep, throwing up. Finally I tell her either we start clearing or she needs to help me get an apartment and I will take the dogs. I woke feeling sick with anxiety and trapped, and had nowhere to go.

I and others are visiting a wealthy family. Besides an immaculate home, they have a huge red barn that has been renovated into a two-story leisure clubhouse. They refer to it as the doghouse. I tell them it is nice enough to be a separate home. I do feel jealous. It is so comfortable and beautiful. We are in a church, and the choir has been placed in different sections around the church – some on the platform, some on the side, some – including me – in the front pews. On the side wall of the platform diagonal from me is a rather large wall decor that resembles a blue hot air balloon. Kim is directing us, and as we begin singing, a dog leaps out of the balloon. I am worried at first, But the dog lands easily on the platform and playfully runs across it.

Nita and I are sitting in a waiting room in the hospital. I have a copy of Ted Dekker's book 'Green' in my lap. I think it belongs to a patient we are seeing. There are fuzzy black balls all over it. I think they are lint. I try to dust some off, some fall to the floor but they multiply. Suddenly the book is covered with fuzzy black balls. I believe they are black mold. We put the book in a heavy ziploc bag, but the mold continues to multiply. I am very disturbed by this.

I am staying in a condo on a beach with white sand and very blue water. Some relatives are staying there with us and they comment that it is much nicer than staying in Mom's house – that her house is too cluttered and smells like she had been sick for a very long time. The room has a king size bed and was very spacious. The window over the head of the bed opens directly onto the beach. There are so many people there it was not so pleasant to look out as you can barely see the water or the sand. Someone sees the window open and brings their baby to look in. A cute little baby (boy I think) is suddenly looking and leaning in the window.

I am watching a rehearsal at A.D. Players. I'm sitting in the dim theatre. I see several people I know on stage, but the only one I clearly recognize is Jen. Jeanette – the character is Jeanette but she is Nita – kindly asks me if I am sure I want to leave. I am smiling sadly and thinking I want to be home and work here; but I am also afraid I will regret it.

I am in the backyard. It is spring. The grass is bright green. Moving something for the garden, I see a small baby snake start to scurry away. Then right next to it, I see a second, then a third, and I think a fourth. I am very concerned for the dogs and fear we have another nest in the yard like last year.

Mom, Des, and I are on vacation (Gatlinburg I think). We are staying in one of the Hunters' homes. To get to it, we have to go through another one of their homes. There is another family staying there. We enter the house, and they are all asleep. A child is sleeping on the couch in the front room. As we go through their rooms to get to the back door, Mom trips and falls backward onto the sleeping mother in this family. There is a smile on her face in sleep. I pull Mom up and we get to the door quickly. But once we are out the back door, I realize one of the dogs is still in the house. I think it is Sox. I begin to call him and a child from that family has awakened and comes to the back door smiling. We apologize to the family for disturbing them and explain we have to go through that house to get to the Hunters' house in which we are staying.

Mom and I are sitting in a table at a restaurant, I think. A lady is standing there talking to us about my debt. She tells me I only have $1000 remaining on 2 credit cards. I am shocked and thrilled. I say I can pay those off in a couple months. I am excited to be facing debt-free living.

I am in the kitchen of Nana's old house, setting the table for a meal. The only person there is Roger. A man comes in who is a friend of his and they begin talking generally. Then the man gestures towards me and says, "And how is she?" From his comments Roger and I both realize suddenly that he thinks I am Connie. Roger asks if he doesn't know I'm his niece, that his wife died. On my way to the freezer, the man asked me to look at him. I do, and he says that I look just like her. I say I get that a lot.

I am on a trip with Mom, Des, the girls, and Stephen. At first I think we're in Louisville, then someone shows me a map with favorite parts of London and asks me where I want to visit as we only have two days left. Not sure of location. There is also a man shopping with me who behaves very familiar and says he's my husband. Not sure who he is. During a retreat part of the trip, John Lattimore is there, talking with another man. They are all in sleeping bags. John says he would do anything go back to work, he would even crawl. I wonder if he asked Lisa for his job back.

I am in a huge store. In one section there is a long kneeling rail and people come there to pray. I witness several people kneel in prayer. I am talking to another person about an organization that helps save babies from being aborted. I tear up a little and apologize, but they encourage me to continue talking about it and celebrate it.

I'm staying late at the hospital. Grigoriyan is there. We have 5 1/2 hamburgers leftover from an event, and we ask him to take them to the children's benefit he is going to. He says it won't do any good, people here are too proud to accept such things. He also says it is very hard on him when one of his patients dies. I tell him that he must learn to accept it is God's timing to take them. He shakes his head in disbelief. I explained that I have experienced it, that I felt the lady's hand being taken out of mine as she passed. He seemed to think about it. I see him the next day in passing as I am working on charts. I want to ask him how the children's benefit went but feel awkward about it, so I say nothing.

There is a man who expressed interest in me. He took me to some seminar about healing one's heart from past hurts, I think. I was surprised that he not only told me about it but with me. He strongly resembled Chip from Houston. However, the man with me in the car on the way back looked very much like Tim, although I could not see his face. At one point I reached out and put my hand in his. However, he took gum out of his mouth and put it in his hand, so not returning the gesture. When he got out of the car and walked away, still not facing me, I thought that I missed him. Later in the hospital I was pondering this man who had spent so much effort trying to get me over the hurt of Tim. I thought I should definitely consider him.

There was a severe accident at the hospital – a man's face had caught on fire and they were taking him to the roof to fly him out. Several of us were going up to witness this, including chaplains. In delirium, the man had injected something into the IV bag which caused his face to spontaneously combust. Lynn Parish drove me to the house where they took him. He said he'd heard I was applying for the Christian school drama position and he would put in a word for me. Rachel and then Connie were both at the house. Connie was hosting many important local people who had come due to the situation. When she saw us arriving, she asked Rachel to get us five glasses and drinks so that we could sit together. Rachel has not spoken to me although she was standing right next to me.

I am at Grace theater. It is dark, preparing for a production. There is an actor there who is extremely charming to me, obviously attentive. He is constantly making me laugh. He's rather heavy – not my usual type – but I do enjoy his company. We go to sit in the seats, and we are talking about various holidays we missed due to being in a show. We both apparently missed quite a few, but enjoyed doing it anyway.

Mom was in the hospital for a simple procedure. But she could not wake up. She's lying in a hospital bed and Jody asks me if I want him to put her on a ventilator. Thinking of our recent conversation, I want to say no. He says they have a new machine and she might come off of it. I look at Mom lying in the bed, not responding.

I have a new job working for a man 10 years my senior who is an undercover detectives. I am attracted to him, at least in thrill of the work if not romantically as well. I am doing an assignment for him. Meeting a suspect at a café, I am disguised with shorter dark hair and a long red coat. As I have the investigating conversation, I look at the teacup on the high table in front of me, lightly touch it with my finger, and imagine how I am going to describe this later. It is almost like a dream within a dream – I know I am dreaming and I know I want to remember it to record it when I wake. I ended the conversation and leave quickly.

I was with a man in an underground lab. It was empty at the time. It was circular and everything was black. Toward the back there was a huge bed with white coverings. I was telling him that this was the doctor's laboratory. Next we were witnessing what went on there. A group of people dressed in period clothing stirred with lust. The doctor was observing them. He encouraged them to start using the bed. One man in pale blue clothing and wearing a long blonde wig approached a woman next to the bed. She said his name scoldingly and yanked the wig off. Then she submissively laid on the bed, raised her skirts, and rolled to her side, indicating he could do whatever he wanted, but she was not reciprocating. I was disgusted.

I bought a birthday cake for a baby who had just turned one. The baby was sitting in a highchair. There was a lady standing next to her and a man standing next to me, but I could not see either of their faces, just the baby's. The other two adults present – probably the baby's parents – were not paying close attention. When I handed the cake to the lady next to the baby, the baby immediately reached from her highchair, quickly pried her hand under the plastic cover, scooped a handful of white icing, and put it in her mouth. After a very brief taste, her expression froze in surprise and delight. The man next to me said it was the first time she had ever had cake.

A man from work has asked me out on a date. I have turned him down. I am alone at home and he calls me. He tells me on the phone that if he were me he would make the bold choice. I ask what that is. He says he would accept his invitation to go out, flowers, dinner, and a wonderful time. He is quite charming and I do decide I want to go out with him. Then something about him makes me nervous and I begin comparing him with Tim. I want to enjoy myself with him, but I'm afraid of making the same mistake again.

I am with a vampire. He is flying – rising straight up in the air, holding me. He seems to believe he is intimidating me. Unafraid, I smile up at him and tell him to do what he needs to do. Then I lightly kiss the side of his neck.

I am at a long picnic table downtown with Mom and several people that seem familiar. Sitting across from me is a new face – a black ballplayer from the college. But he seems my age rather than college. Among his selections he has a small iron skillet of what looks like homemade cornbread. I express delight that it reminds me of my grandmother. He agrees, and Mom and I take a picture of him with it, to send to his family. Later he is driving a car and I am in the passenger seat next to him. A white female friend is in the back and she has had something to annoy him; he is angry, refusing to talk. She keeps asking what she said but he won't answer. As she persists I wish she would just let it go. I reach over and begin to rub his hair and forehead in attempt to sooth him.

I was driving a car and Luke was beside me. We were on North Mayo Trail, passing the bridge near my old house. For a moment I seemed it to combine him with Joe – Kelly's husband from ADPlayers (odd, as I dreamed about Kelly at ADPlayers last night). I asked him if he didn't miss working in theatre. Then we were at a theatre, and it was obviously Luke. We were at a back side wall of the theatre and preparation for a production was underway. The lights were dim. He began kissing me, lightly at first then deeply. He asked if I wanted to go for coffee. I told him I thought we were past coffee. He hummed an agreement in my mouth. He felt wonderful.

I was at the St. Street annex at ADPlayers in Houston. I was walking around the downstairs, talking with everyone I still new and enjoying myself. Then I went upstairs. The sunlight was spilling in. With anticipation and joy, I went into the PR office. The desks were as they were when I left. Kelly was there, and she jumped up to hug me. She seemed much older. She was in charge of several new players, all very young. I had only happy thoughts being there.

There was an obnoxious little girl and her mother in our backyard. They were at the level of my window. Although it seemed sunny outside, the window was open and rain was coming in. I saw two men in black suits – like the typical men in black of the mothman stories – come and lead the little girl away. She did not want to go with them and began whining in protest. Her mother became scared. Then a third man, this one in work clothes like a beige coverall and matching blank cap, was at the window talking to the mother. He was facing me, her back was to me. He was smiling and seemed to be encouraging her to let the men take her daughter. He appeared condescending if not mildly threatening. She ran after them. On the inside of the window, I watched while drying the headboard of my bed with a cloth where the rainwater had splattered it.

I am with a group of people at the hospital and an attractive man who works with us – transport I think – approaches and begins to talk to me. He is wearing a red jacket, and he stands close to me and is rather flirtatious. My hand is resting on the back of a chair and he keeps touching it and rubbing my fingers with his. I am shocked at his outwardness, but very attracted to him.

I am attending a dying patient. She cannot talk, but continues to gesture towards her open purse on the table, directing me to get something out of it. I bring the purse to her bed, but she cannot go through it herself. I open it, then go to the hall to ask for someone to witness me. I think there is a Bible in it.

A patient's last wish was to drink coffee. She was a very frail elderly woman, thin with white hair. For her comfort care, we put her in a clear tank which had a coffee brewing system on top. She was arranged in a seated position with her head tilted back and fresh hot coffee streamed into her open mouth all day and night. When she was still alive the next morning (there was a flower sitting in water next to her and we knew that she was breathing if air bubbles came up out of the flower) I was very concerned. I told Nita her mouth and throat would be scalded if she continued to have hot coffee poured into her. Nita to said if we moved her it would disturb her. I fearfully watched the lady in the tank with great anxiety but did not know what to do.

3 dreams last night: 3 I am taking garbage out of the kitchen. I have a huge trash bag full of garbage. For some reason, I have thrown my Brita pitcher into it. I suddenly realize I need the filter out of it. I reach into take it out, but the filter already has garbage around it, so I put it back in together. I am afraid if Mom sees me taking out all the garbage she will try to go through it. I see Church at the backdoor and ask Mom if she wants him to come in. It seems strange that he is outside as he was always an indoor cat. I asked her if she wants him to be an inside cat.

Stephen – or someone exactly like him – was working at the hospital. I had to work around him, suffering being in love with him and not being able to express it. I wanted to leave. I was standing at the old main lobby entrance and he passed me in the hall. I watched him go and hated the ache in my chest.

I was on a sled gliding between houses. Clay was resting on my chest like he used to do when he was a baby. I thought, he's too big for this now. When we got to the house, he was very tired and I told him he could lie down on my bed for a nap, but all four dogs were lying on my bed. The bedspread was black and gold horizontal zigzag. I thought it was very ugly.

I am dating a much younger man; at least he seems much younger – rather immature. He looks to be in his 20s maybe. I come to believe he is a serial killer. I am planning to separate from him, but I go by his room and find my mother and his mother sitting on his floor going through boxes under his bed – souvenirs he has kept from his kills – searching for evidence. They tell me I have to distract him so he doesn't walk in on them. To keep him out of the room I satisfy him by having sex with him. It feels unnatural and disgusting. It is in a completely white room on the floor. I tell myself I have to do it so they can find proof.

Deb and Jeff had gotten married. They had just found out they were pregnant. Deb was not happy. I was watching them in their kitchen, but it was as if they didn't see me. Jeff looked frustrated, sad. Dad looked angry, irritated. They weren't talking to or facing each other.
