In the beginning she was a copper-brown horse. She had long reigns and I was standing on a type of sled behind her. She took off up a mountain trail quickly. It was frightening, exhilarating, freeing. But as we came to a shelter at the top of the hill, the horse became Nyla. She was still running, pulling me on the sled. Suddenly a coyote ran out and took a vicious stance as if to attack her; then another one joined it. I was scared for her and wanted off the sled to get to her.

I was getting ready for work and wanted to check my hair. I walked into Mom's room to look in her dresser mirror. Mom was lying on her bed with Major. The room was clear and clean. The sheets were light and clean. The room was open and comfortable.

I am on the bypass with Nyla. We have a house there. I need to walk down the street, but I'm afraid she will follow me and get hurt. I start to walk along the sidewalk and she obediently stays on the property. Then Mom drives up and Nyla runs into the road to circle her car. I go back to make sure she is safe.

Des tells us that she and Will have decided to try to work things out. For the next two weeks he will be living in the house with her and the girls again. She told us we had to accept it. There is someone sitting on the couch next to her listening but I do not know who and they never speak. Chris, her current boyfriend, is serving at her table, silently. I am horrified that she is going to let Will back it. She will not listen to any of us. I want to tell her if she is foolish enough to take him back that he needs to pay her attorney bill instead of Mom having to do it. I am scared for her and the girls.

I am on a bus trip to New York City. Just outside of the city, we stop for tea at a hotel café, and I am drawn into conversation with another girl on the bus. She is wearing a long coat. After we have tea together, we continue on our trip into New York.

One – church leaders were celebrating the birth of Brad's grandchild by showing a slideshow of images that had absolutely nothing to do with a baby or anything else. Everyone was rather confused, including Brad. When church let out, I was surprised to see an older Tiffany escorting two handicap youths out of an aisle in front of me. She was wearing a dress and looked back and smiled but did not speak as she left.

I was in Richard's office. I had just learned that Danny had committed suicide. I knew Richard was devastated because Danny had been a friend and protégé (only in dream – not even sure if they know each other). He was very sad. He sat at his desk, picked up the phone, and called Danny. To my surprise, Danny answered, and they began to talk as if having a counseling session. Both seemed happy enough. Sitting across the desk from him, and hearing the whole conversation, I wondered how he could be talking to Danny after his death; also if there was then something we could do to stop his death.

I was in a massive old hotel. I was walking through the lobby, and was suddenly very aware of a spirit's presence. I slowed slightly and quietly said, "You may go now." Then I walked on. I felt confident and at peace.

I am on a retreat with a few other ministers from various walks. We are in a huge room in a house talking together one afternoon. I am comfortably sitting on the floor looking out the windows. One wall facing out is entirely glass, and a storm is brewing. It is very beautiful. We are talking about playing a card game – possibly rook. We are sharing our stories on how we came to this particular retreat. A man in the group says that pain brought us together. I don't know these people but I feel very comfortable and peaceful with them.

I am in Nana's old house. Jeanette is there. She is in a rage and we are arguing. I am standing up to her. I hand her a resignation notice until her I am through. I start out the front door. I hear her coming behind me. I turned to see her running out the front door chasing me. She is screaming, I will never let you leave! I shout back, I've already left! I turn and continue walking across my family's former mutual yard. There is a tree in front of me with pretty pink flowers.

I was at a Christian conference. I ran into Beth Moore in the bathroom like I used to in Houston. I didn't think she would remember me, but I asked her if she still attended First Baptist Church in Houston. She repeated it as a question as if she did not know what church or city I meant. Outside in the grassy field at a table I saw Jeanette at a book signing. I clearly saw the title of the book but I cannot remember it now. It had a cream-colored background, darker circle on the front of it-very plain. Jeanette looked weary and miserable. Her hair was falling out. What was left was very stringy and hanging everywhere. I spoke kindly to her and she grabbed a copy of the book and autographed the front of it to me. Then she got up and hugged me. I felt so sorry for her and all I could feel for her was forgiveness.

I was looking at a mauve colored sheet of paper that was a memorial. The list of names appeared to be healthcare workers who had recently died, apparently in the line of duty. There was the name of the road beside each name listed, the road on which they died, along with the dates of their lives in years. At the bottom of the page, I saw a woman who had died on Sydney Road. For some reason, Sydney Road struck me. I felt sad when I read it, I said it out loud – "She died on Sydney Road." I started to cry when I said it. Then I looked at the name listed to the left of the road. It was me. I looked at the dates to the right. 1973 - 2013. I was surprised. That year is already over, I thought. In my minds eye, the three began to morph into a 14. That's right, I thought. Then I woke up.

Stephen. The dream was all about him. I was in Houston with him, in theatre auditions with him. We were supposed to do a scene together and it kept getting postponed. We worked on scenes with others. We were auditioning outside, on a grassy field with tables and tents. It was a beautiful day, warm, sunny, clear blue sky. I don't know if I ever spoke directly to him. I was hurt and angry. I felt so much yearning for him but was angry that I had to be there. He kept coming very close to me, laughing, talking to others, very near me but never touching. Once we were sitting on opposite sides of the table and he leaned across the table and reached right past me, inches away from me, but I could not bring myself to simply stretch out my hand and touch him. Restraint, so much restraint.

I am in Houston. A homeless ministry is ministering to Chip. He is in a flimsy shelter that appears to be a structure of boards with white plastic attached. He seems quite content, confident, in good spirits. I wonder if he has had a falling out with Jeanette, and if he has lost his job with ADPlayers and therefore his home.

I was on an investigation tour with the ghost adventures guys. Zak was in a particularly foul mood, and, in our motel room, took out a knife and began to cut my feather pillow. I told him to stop. He did not – he sliced it from one corner down the side to the next corner. He said it was too old for his taste, and I should have gotten a new one. I was going to explain to him that now I'm a vegetarian and will not be purchasing another feather pillow. It was rather irritating.

It is raining hard this morning, flooding around us. In waking sleep, I thought I may need to walk the big dogs on leashes today rather than have them get muddy in the backyard. Instantly I dreamed I was looking out my bedroom window and saw a stranger dressed in a black suit with white shirt standing at the back right corner of the chain-link fence, looking in the yard. He was thin and bald. I think he wore glasses. Then I was walking Nyla and Major down the street. As I passed the neighbors', I saw the same man looking in their fence on the far side of their house. I tried to remember if I had brought my phone with me. It was in my pocket. I took it out and quickly took photos of the man. Then I pocketed the phone and asked if I could help him. He looked at me, and I woke up.

Mom was doing something (I think w/Des & girls) & asked me to take her car home & walk the dogs. When I got to the door, I realized Mom had the house keys--they were not in her car. I was aggravated & wondered how I was going to get in. Then I thought, Nana & Dadi have a spare key at their house. Happily, I ran across the yards to their house, knowing they would be there, knowing they would have a key. I was happy I would get to see them.

Des is living here in the house with me. Tony Goldwin is here with us, and he is showing me particular interest. He is very kind and very helpful. He is also extremely well-built and good looking. Des and I are folding laundry in the hallway and I toss a clothes hanger behind me. He immediately retrieves it. Des is making fun of an Italian pinstriped dark suit he is wearing, but I say that I like the suit, and the six pack underneath it.

I had moved back to Houston to be with Stephen. I was going to rejoin the Players and tell him I still loved him. When I got there I discovered Tiffany had moved there and was trying to go out with him. I knew she wasn't really interested in him, but she said she was going to go out with him. I warned him that she would break his heart.

Dr. Bartley was showing me a bright red very expensive car. He said it cost approximately $435,000. Then he laughed and said he had four of them. I wondered what in the world he was doing buying the same 4 cars.

I was sitting on a concrete structure, similar to a park area. There was water in front of me and some sort of reservoir. Behind me, there was what looked like a natural pond surrounded by glass. I was lamenting not working in theater anymore and feeling very dissatisfied with my current work. Suddenly I've's huge frog leapt behind me. It had bright yellow wings – flimsy and flappy – that flapped as it hopped. It bounced along behind me across the grass and jumped into the pond. I felt like God was telling me I was supposed to be working with animals.

I was on my way to check the mail, and there was a small snake – red with black rings – at the side of the ports. At the front of the porch. Every time I try to take a step it moves toward me. At one point it looks so quickly I actually stepped on it. It raised his head on the other side of my shoe. I started to run for the mailbox And the snake followed me. Again every time I took a step it came at me. I ran back to the house, it chasing me the whole way, and finally made it back to the porch, upon which it did not come.

Nana and that I were on a trip and I was checking their house for them. They had a dog and a cat who were out of food. I took a key I had and let myself into their garage, found dog, cat and bird food, and fed the dog and cat. Afterwards, I went around the front of the house and was writing something on the note at their front door. One of the Neighbors called to me and asked if I was some sort of salesgirl. I ignored them.

I was in a spa setting with the cast of the walking dead. I was talking to David about his acting and he asked what I did. I expressed that are used to be in Christian actress, missed it very much, but now worked as a vet chaplain for animals. Some people were in pain and I told them with all the energy workers around they should have some work done.

I was in the room of a very sick patient. Jason was talking to the patient's relative about end-of-life care. The woman said she wanted the patient to be euthanized. There was a wall of cages behind us full of dogs. I thought the patient on the bed was a dog but then it turn into an old man. I questioned the lady's choice, that this patient's illness was so inconvenient she wanted to kill him. She ignored me; she had made her decision.

I was in Houston, at A.D. Players. Nita it was with me as well as several other ladies. Nita a wanted to go to the afternoon performance of the children's show. She thought if we all went together we would only have to pay about one dollar each and was frustrated when she was told we would each be charged six dollars for admission. I did not want to be there. I was uncomfortable thinking I would run into Stephen. I went backstage, met some of the actors, recognized non of them, looked at costumes and backstage things, then went to the audience. After we were seated, I began to fear he might be in the play we were about to watch. I did not want to see him.

I was at the front porch of the little yellow house here in Pikeville. Tiffany was there, and she brought me a letter that hospice had sent me accusing me of being her partner, and therefore unworthy to offer spiritual guidance. It said we had been together since high school and that we still lived together. I thought I needed to tell them I lived with my mother. The letter was five pages long and included video sections Inside the paper that showed scenes from my high school years in which I was supposedly looking at her with attraction. I tried to remember if one of them was working through her during those times. But whatever information they had was certainly from the past, not present, and had not been directed toward her. The last page asked me to sign my signature, admitting guilt. Feeling sad and overwhelmed with guilt from the past, I refused to sign and was going to contact them.

Tom had to piled firewood from the side of their house to ours, blocking our gate into the backyard. He and mom were talking. Rhoda and I were standing in the front yard on a deck-like platform, just looking around and listing to them. Mom asked him a question about property lines, and he said he didn't know, she told him where to put things. For a moment I thought he meant Marsha Kowalski, but he indicated by gesture Rhoda. Sox and Scout had climbed on top of his woodpile and were working the latch on the gate. Sox would push up on one end while Scout pushed down on the other and they were about to open the latch. I thought, amused and concerned, even if we could not use the gate to get into the backyard, they could still use it to get out.

I am in the hospital room of a patient who has died. (It is a patient who has been dying slowly and then pain because his wife would not allow him to be given proper pain medication.) The patient is lying in bed dead. The wife is sitting in a chair beside the bed, facing the foot. She is dressed in all gray and is sobbing. I am standing at the foot of the bed facing her. There is a nurse standing behind me. She begins begging the nurse, "Check the window to see if it's cold outside." The nurse starts towards the window and I wake up. I feel the urge to touch the window glass to see if it is cold.

I am working in ICU. Dr. Grigoriyan is there. He is dressed in his black scrubs and holding an open black umbrella over his head. I ask him why he has the umbrella. He doesn't answer, just smiles. In the center of the unit is a glass enclosure. There is a patient in isolation inside. The only way to access the enclosure is a sliding glass door. The patient seems somewhat uneasy about being in the isolated enclosure. She is up and walking; I don't know why she is in there. go in to visit her and have some trouble sliding the door open. Others comment and I laugh and say I've never opened the door before.

Mom is telling me to get off work because she has planned a vacation in Gatlinburg. She wants us to stay in the cabin. I am frustrated because she has already made the plans without waiting to see if I can get off for letting me know about them. I ask her if she has contacted the cabin owners and she says no. I feel angry and disappointed that she would plan the trip without talking to me first or making any arrangements.

I am at church, I think for special event. We are in the choir loft getting ready to sing, but several choir members are missing, including ones we thought were to join us. Kim is at the front getting ready to direct, and I find I am the only soprano present. I look around and notice how very small our choir is and wonder if we can pull off the songs.

Thursday, October 17 Penny and I were walking through a park in the woods. We stopped to sit at a bench along the path and saw a young hawk flying low overhead. I got up to watch it and it swooped down to me and I caught it in my arms. It was white and amazingly soft. I held it very comfortably for some time before letting it go. Then it sailed away, back up into the sky. It was an amazing sensation.

10/12/13 Sat Nita & I were taking some1 around the hospital. I think they were interviewing to work with us. They asked us questions about PMC. We got into an elevator & were surprised to find the wall panels removed, leaving a see-through barrier that enabled riders to see throughout the shaft as they traveled. It was interesting but somewhat frightening. I wondered why they didn't set it out so riders could see pretty scenery or at least the hospital areas rather than all the gears & cords of the shaft. Later this day, Mom & I toured the Jim Beam distillery. The gift shop elevator was round, resembling a barrel. The inside walls were only hard metal mesh, & portholes like barrel holes were placed at certain levels, so you could see all around the shaft as you traveled.

There was a toilet on the street in town. It was completely out in the open, sitting on the sidewalk. I was using it, and I had papers in my hand – maybe newspapers – and I was talking on my cell phone. People were walking by as if it was totally normal for others to use the toilet openly. Then a man and his father approached me. The man began to touch me inappropriately and I shouted for him to stop. I still had the papers and was still talking on the phone. With his father standing near him, he drug me off the toilet, shoved me to the concrete, and was about to rape me. The passersby stopped and watched, but no one helped. Then I saw as if through his eyes, but I could see no one on the ground. I knew I was seeing him raping me but I was invisible.

I was talking with a patient's family at the hospital. They were discussing their family tree with me and we discovered that the patient had a young son no one realized in the family. Later I was talking to Nana. We were discussing our family tree. I found the birth of a young boy in her family line. I asked her if she had ever had a son and was surprised when she said yes. I asked Mom later if she was aware she had a baby brother. I think the son had died at an early age and Mom and Connie did not know about him.

I walked out of a building into a parking lot where my car was parked. There was a red car parked next to mine. A gas hose hung from the red car to my car. The red car was sucking the gas out of my car. A voice said, "Someone is sucking your energy." I woke frightened, feeling threatened.

I am in a restaurant. Dad is there with me. He picks me up like I am a small child and spins me around, making my feet fly out in front of me. I have on bright yellow shoes. I think what an odd thing to do for an adult child, but ponder that he must need to express such playful, loving fatherly expression. We go outside of the restaurant. It is a bright, sunny day, blue skies and bright green grass. Mom is in the grassy field where cars are parked. I hate that they have run into each other, but it is pleasant and not stressful. As dad is getting into the car he is talking to Mom and appears very sad. She asks simply, "Is it still hard to say goodbye?" He says, "It is always hard to say goodbye to you." I know that Beth is in the car, wonder if Mom has met her, and wonder what he means.

Our fenced-in yard and the creekside beyond were the same, but distorted in size, seeming to span more space than in reality. I am about to take Nyla and Major for a walk, but I put them on their Y leash. Beyond the fence on the other side of the creek bed is a shewolf, lying in the leaves on the mountainside. She is huge, and I am in awe of how beautiful she is, but worried about her harming the dogs if she can reach them. I keep them on the leash and stay in the backyard with them. The pups are loose and running, barking. I plan to bring them indoors. The wolf is calmly looking around her surroundings, apparently uninterested in the dogs or myself.

I was working in a theater, here in town. I was walking through the backstage area behind the main curtain (deep red velvet) with two other people. We saw three others coming towards us and they crossed us in passing. I noticed the one in the middle was Tom Cruise wearing a black hooded cloak. I could barely distinguish his face. As my two companions & I waited (they were sitting, I was standing) on the stage right wing just beyond the curtain, he came back through the passage behind the curtain to where we were. He was pacing, mumbling something to himself. He was still wearing the black cloak with the hood. It occurred to me with amused irony that he was trying to pray. With sincerity & some amusement I asked, "Sir, would you like me to pray for you?" He stopped pacing and mumbling, looked at me for a moment, then looked down and said no, he didn't believe in it anyway. Then he disappeared into the dark behind the curtain again.

Tim was back in town. But he was completely different than before. He was mature, responsible, kind. He was teaching two classes for an attorney dealing with law at the University. He had plenty of money. He was very kind and respectful to me when we met, and he wanted to be around me a lot after realizing I was still here. He said he knew I had been praying for him the whole time he was away, he had felt the prayers and was very grateful for them. He insisted on paying for everything, was extremely respectful of my space. I found myself being fearful of a setback, but also feeling an old attraction for him. After a lunch date, we were sitting on a park bench together, and sitting very closely I initiated a kiss with him. It felt strange. He was very tender, again respectful, but I feared it would be the same as before.

Dr. Grigoriyan is telling me something about a patient we are working on together. It seems very important, but I'm disturbed during the dream, wake up, and cannot remember what it is. I think it's about a patient we discussed yesterday.

I answer a tent. A woman and her daughter, a young child, I do not know inch or behind me. The tent is fairly spacious, brown. It's dim inside. The floor is dirt, dry dirt, dust. There are four cots spaced around the tent. On the cots are 4 men. 2 of the bodies are covered. They are dead. One appears to be dead but the blanket has not been pulled over his face yet. The 4th man looks dead at first, but then he starts groaning. He says the man in the cot next to him is his father. I am horrified that these people have been abandoned to die alone in this place. I try to comfort the man. I wonder why I am there.

Mom & I were looking for a hotel. It was getting late, already dark. We didn't know the town but were happy to be staying there. We saw a huge, old, red brick hotel. It was right next to a funeral home, so close they appeared to be against one another. The hotel was so historic & grand, we decided to stay there for the night. When we had checked in & the staff was leading us to our room, they brought us to large, metal double doors which they swung open, revealing a stark, unpleasantly bright empty hallway; & I realized in terror that they were taking us into the funeral home. But we were led down another hall to the right, & it was richly furnished in deep red carpet & draperies around many doors. I exclaimed it must have been an old movie house. I was very uncomfortable when I woke from this dream.

We are at a church picnic. K is sitting across from us, as he did at the recent church picnic. He is eating 2 chicken legs. But as he takes a bite, a joint in the leg starts to move. The leg is "kicking." He looks scared & comments the chicken wasn't dead. It is very frightening to watch.

Mom & I were trying to help Des with her dogs. After she came into the enclosure with us, she grabbed her chest & collapsed. Some1 began doing cpr on her. It may have been me. During the pause, I looked up at Tori who was standing on the deck crying & watching her mother. I was afraid my sister was dead.

Happy was in Pikeville. I was spending the day with him. He got a flat tire while we were driving, so we went looking for a garage that was open. 1 man (familiar but not sure who he is) was on the st Granny used to live on. He said we could look quickly but the garage was closing soon. We were in a grassy yard; the garage he referred to was a concrete block shed with some tires & tools along it. I whispered that he owned the place, thinking if funny he was so eager to close when we could hive him some business. We went to an auto shop with tires handing from the walls. As we looked around, I took his arm. I vaguely thought he might be with someone else, but I wasn't concerned. I knew we were meant to be together & would be from this day on.

Mom was telling me that she had been praying for people near death & they were miraculously healed. All of them, apparently. Seems it had been going on a long time. "I bring them back from the brink," she said almost casually. 2 things occurred to me at once--yea, 3, as Dekker would say. 1, that's very nice that God uses Mom's prayers to heal people & give them more time. 2, I felt she was a little full of herself as she talked about it. 3, how does that happen since Mom has not prayed aloud for years?

I was rehearsing a play with Lee. He was not a lead role (I think I was) but he had created such a fun character, it was delightful to watch him while he worked. He made the character appear small--hunched over with a high voice--interesting, delightful. He wore a dark red coat & dark brown pants of rough material, burlap maybe, & a short pointed hat with a wide brim, straw-like. He was like a cute little hermit who lived in the woods, very wise yet completely light-hearted. I was on a stage platform watching him & laughing quietly with delight. I thought of Mom & how she would like the show when she came & hoped she would like seeing him. It felt wonderful to be working on stage.

I went to Houston for a visit to the old theatre & my friends there. Literally overnight, Stephen married Ashley Vanhoose (a childhood schoolmate). I had no idea why she was even there, & no 1 knew they were even dating. But they met us for a meal, announcing they were newlyweds. I felt miserable. I felt he was the love of my life & just when we might have reconnected I lost him to some1 I hadn't heard of since hs graduation. Horrible emotional suffering.

I was sleeping on my twin Tempurpedic mattress on the driveway. It was next to the garage door. My head was toward the road, feet toward the porch. It was daylight. I woke to see 2 huge black snakes crawling side by side along the driveway, from the patio area towards the front yard. I was scared. They were such large, bloated creatures. I knew I had to get rid of them, but had no idea how.

The day after I had this dream, I saw Dr M at the hospital. He was in jeans & a buttoned shirt, not his usual scrubs. It was his day off, but he was there, & seemed stressed. As we (Nita & I) entered an elevator with him, he told us he was being sued. I was shocked--not only due to the recent dream, but because he is a very careful & caring dr & I cannot imagine him in a situation in which some1 would try to sue him. Still, so many ignorant people in this area do so at the drop of a hat.

I was called to take the family of a deceased patient to the morgue to view the body. I advised against it, but they insisted. All the way, I felt dread. I didn't want to go there, but felt I had to for the family. When we arrived, an attendant uncovered the body. It was horrifying. The eyes & mouth were wide open in a grimace of terror. There was black around the teeth, the tongue protruded, the hair (long, bleachy blond) was wild & frizzy. The arms & hands were drawn under the face as if extreme pain. The family began crying immediately. I tried not to react, but I took several slow steps back, then turned away. Suddenly a security guard was standing at the door--a tall, hefty woman with short blond hair. She said she was there to watch the family & I could go if I wanted. I asked if she was sure. & I left. I woke with that horrible image in my mind.

A handsome stranger asked me to marry him in order to have a baby. I agreed, due to age & desire for marriage. I was timid on our wedding night, but comfortable with him. He was beautiful & delighting. He was an extremely kind, gentle, providing man. He spent much time out of town, so I was often alone; but completely provided for. I felt so safe knowing I was with him. There was a party in town, & he came home to attend. I entered the room, beautifully dressed in satiny white, & saw him across the room, talking to some men. I smiled, secretly delighted to belong to him, & started down the short set of stairs to cross the crowd & join him.

The Methodist Church had become a megachurch. The sanctuary was a large, spacious, bright (lots of long, clear windows) room, big enough for a couple thousand people. Brad was preaching, & he was enjoying it. He rapped the last part of his sermon, & we were all clapping & laughing. I tried to text Mom that he was rapping a sermon; thought it would amuse her. After church service, we had a church family lunch. At least 2 whole tables of food were set up, maybe more. On 1 table I found veggie-chilli; veggie burgers on another. I was surprised & grateful they had specially provided for me. It was too much for me to eat alone, & I didn't want to disappoint anyone. But others were enjoying it too. Brad ate a veggie burger himself, & told another older man he should try it, which he did. I felt a good sense of community, church family; I had a place among them.

Mom was trying to convince me I needed to have Nyla put down. I of course refused. We were at the kitchen door, letting Nyla run into the backyard with Scout & Sox (did not see Major). Mom said she knew I wouldn't agree to do it here, & we needed to get ready to go to Lex. I was sad & angry. I wasn't going to do it & wanted her to stop pressing it. Nyla was happy & seemed healthy, running & playing with the Terriers.

I was trying to match the 'snow blue' wall paint in my room to buy some new paint. I was showing my wall to someone who was helping me select a purchase. "This is 'snow blue,'" I was saying, showing them the wall. They had in their colors a 'snow flake blue' & I thought it was close.

A man was torturing a horse. He had cut its face & attached a horn to make it look like a unicorn. He had the horn & wound covered with a wire mesh to keep the horn attached until it was fixed in place. The horse was screaming. I was horrified, disgusted. I had to find a way to free & save the animal.

I knew Happy was in town. I wanted to call him, because I knew talking with him would bring me joy. I called him (he didn't call me) & was badly surprised when Tiff's sister answered the phone. I asked to talk to Happy. I heard her say I was a snob as she handed off the phone. He answered. He seemed happy to talk with me, but I had to come to that house. I did. It was very uncomfortable. I didn't feel happy, I felt angry & dirty.

Uncle Maurice had had a stroke I think. He was in a rehab facility, working to get his speech back. He could only repeat 2 sentences but he was happy & doing well. Mom didn't want to go see him & I couldn't understand why. I was trying to talk her into visiting him.

Mom, Dadi & I were in a riddle match {'the Hobbie'?} with Freddy Kruger, the goal of which was to free a trapped soul. There was a white sheet of paper on which we had to draw our answers in black ink. (Freddy was invisible of course & his black scratches appeared hand unseen.) The 3rd & last riddle I think was I had to draw the trapped soul's way to freedom. I let the pen flow & drug it down (like Bob Ross does with the paint knife) to quickly form a deep, black door. Freddy's response came in scratched words at the bottom of the page: You're dead, Tackett. I was paranoid all day, looking behind me constantly, until I suddenly was sucked into a dream world, & I saw him right in front of me. Like those crazy dreams I had as a horror movie fanatic teen, I wasn't afraid of him. He touched me & I let him. We came together as though reuniting.

I was walking thru the alley to go into the Methodist church. I saw Brad in the street at the corner & called out to him; but as soon as he turned I forgot what I meant to tell him. He met me in the middle of the alley & said he wanted to start an early church service. Everyone would have to be there no later than 6:35am, & he was doing away with the later service. I was explaining to him that 6:30 was far too early when Nyla woke me to throw up. No conclusion. No ideas.

I was visiting Houston & Jeff wanted to show me his new house. It was several levels--5 I think. The 1st floor was spacious, bright & open. The space narrowed each level we ascended. It was very unusual in the middle part. I remember one area that was an indoor garden--rich, black soil with dark green plants growing in it, & a pole where a little dog was relieving himself. {I think this is from the ground cover I planted at the steps, & a cartoon I saw last night of a dog bragging he could pee indoors on a Christmas tree.} The top level, most narrow of all, was difficult to enter. We climbed a stair ladder to get into it. The floor was little more than a few planks with mauve carpet set on them. We had to stretch out on our stomachs to be in the space & talk. We soon went back down.

There are visitors on the campus of MSU, going from department to department, seeing different demonstrations. Each dept is offering a specialized attraction. The visitors are in suits. They look formal, business-like. I am rehearsing for a show on the Kibby stage, preparing for the theatre demonstration. We dance on the stage--back steps, flowing costumes, skirts streaming red, purple, blue. I can see the visitors walking across the lawn, as if in my mind, & wonder if we will be in make-up & ready in time. I am sitting in the green rm, recalling all the shows from my past that brought me to this rm. I think about going to the bathrm to dress as I always did; then think, my body is fine, & decide to change there with the others. We are ready. The audience is arriving.

Deb & I were discussing (long distance--messaging) a movie we had seen. I couldn't remember the name of it, but finally recalled "Benjamin or Ben Lewis" in the title. It was a sort of blend of Edward "Scissorhands" & "Twilight." {Edward both. Jane Eyre?} It was rather juvenile in plot but made me feel that twinge that it was ok to love again.

When I asked him to stay, he said there was all this stuff (3 bags of things next to the bed) that had to be put away. He left me alone in bed & started working on with the bags. I felt horrible-- rejected insecure abandoned betrayed unlovable--my husband left me after making love for the 1st time lazy--why didn't I have the desire to get up & sort/clear bags? I wanted to lie in bed & hold each other. dirty--why were the bags there in the 1st place? Was I hoarding?

First, all men - age range from college to rickety, silver-haired ones. They do their spartan dance, sexy. Then the music opens and their crew grows to men and woman. The captain is a woman- her role: to inspire community in all of the families. I am the only spectator and offer my lonesome applause when they finish.

I am traveling, travelers. Yoga and back-packs. Nice crowd. I find myself in partnership with Carter. We are driving, he is holding me, right arm around me so tightly, my feet are practically in the driver's area. It feels good and secure and loving. I make sure he can drive ok. He seems proud and loving, caring protective. We are in a smaller indoor space. He is meeting with friends, I am doing sudoku on a small coffee table on the side. I am shirtless, the heat is heavy. A man comes and starts asking me questions. I hesitate to turn around, to show my breasts any more vulnerably. Then, another man is sprinkling water and I reach my face towards him, to experience that refreshment. Carter is there and giving that man angry-man eyes, possessive, this-is-my-woman eyes. I ask for it. Permission is granted and I feel the cool, refreshing sprinkles on my face.

Night time & down the hill, I associate with a group that I am somewhat responsible for. Zaneta is in the mix and needs a level of aloofness to be held in check. I am in line for the make-up artists. The space is vast. We are inside, but the outside is a lawn that stretches out & around. A roller coaster, roller-snapper emerges. The rails unhook, whip around and hook back on. Movements like birds of prey.

Crowds in school buildings, personal growth community, I share the CITO recordings, especially for Poland but not in Polish. I go upstairs, to a large and spacious classroom where people are collecting their year of art. Lovely Mrs.B. my friend is packing and wraps glass birds up in newspaper, for their spots in the traveling box. I feel confident and fine because we all have god systems in place.

We are in a gym, a crowd at a conference. Older fellas in biker jackets hang with each other and talk slowly as I zip around in my way - collecting necessary details. I go through a pile of clothing, like the cat suits of anatomy, relevant somehow to my work. There is some people-shuffling, some need to put out fires, tend to people's comfort and well being. But I am only so engaged.

Rickshaws, I am on the back with another man. Vilde had been driving us the few blocks from the park to the clinic. Another rickshaw is with us - with Elizabeth and her toddler. We get to the building - gray and bunker-like. Vilde goes to help the others descend, Brigit hops on our rickshaw and drives us to the next door. Inside, scheduling... Gray and dank, small desks like for taking tests, muddled light.

Renata Beata had dinner at my place and insisted on leaving with her dirty plates, to wash them at home. I want them back from her. She gets into the elevator, holding the plates. We ride down together. Finally, at the ground floor, we see other politicians, in tuxedos, and she gets self conscious enough to return the plates. I get into another part of the elevator and select 11, to go home. On the way up, we pass other floors - apartments with open doors, people in life. My neck hurts from the way I am carrying my purse.

I am dancing at the Hessler Street Fair. Naked, covered maybe in mud or paint or dough. I close my eyes and follow the river of people. I make it to the end of the street in a matter of seconds. I am surprised at the speed, my familiarity, the relative comfort of being naked in this group. I am put of breath, exhausted, hurt in the right shoulder from the intense, African dance I just finished. On arrival, I pull a small shower on a short white hose out of my bag. There is a tool bag on the floor. I take a screwdriver and get to work, putting the shower on the faucet. There are several settings of tightness. It takes several attempts to get the pressure right and we all can wash.

We land at a high security airport, which has the planes unload miles away from the terminal. We are unloaded and transferring to the building. Thousands of tiny workers are circling in on the wheel or baggage hatch or wing. So tiny that I fear crushing half a dozen of them just by stepping forward. I pick one up and smash his minute body and machine in the gesture of my thumb and index finger. I alert my friend.

In the dream, I wake up at Vilde's (we are). He is alert, awake, eager to get going. It is 6 am and I need to leave by 8 (I do). I'd rather sleep a little longer. He is wearing a blue suit, white shirt, and is really excited about going out to buy a special cable for his computer. I stay to sleep. There are paper clouds with angel-hair streamers all over his ceiling. The attic is not quite his- a tad more magical, theatrical, mysterious, purple.

Cube alarm clock with so many settings. I set the address book. I set the color saturation. Spiderman's red and blue becomes redder and bluer. Like a TV screen I watch an ad for radio Zet and admire the lighting. I don't recognize the star, her close-ups reveal imperfections in her skin. she is Polish and speaks to the viewer with enthusiasm and excitement. I'm standing next to Jeremy he greets me with a long, lip to lip kiss. Julie is watching from across the table, rolls her eyes and says, "really, again?" and then she needs help with the baby. Jeremy ands the baby to her, tumbling him like a football.

A woman who is my aunt in the dream is over-eager to clean up the table, taking my unfinished plate several times, stacking it under another plate so that my food is actually 'dirty' from the top plate. The second time, I tell her- that Im not done and I don't appreciate it. She says sorry, removed the top plate. By then I've lost my appetite.

I make an offer to a group of strangers. The light is gentle sunny, wooden floors. // There is shooting. Bullets like rain. I navigate the "storm" without much fear. I use my hand to block their flow. I am well.

Thrive. It takes me three hours to explain what I do to the woman sitting next to me at the diner. She finally gets it and lights up. In conversation with another woman, she's is that's what I'm here for - to clarify. It's like an apartment, objects on windowsills. I go into the meeting room & sit next to Colleen. I ask her if she knows the other Colleen, the yoga teacher and I'm surprised to find out she doesn't. Within minutes that Colleen shows up and I bring them together: Colleen meet Colleen. The one who is silly, speaking and accents, speaks in accents. Then there's some confusion about my seat, which I stood up from to make the introduction. Someone from the back tries to take it but I shuffle around and reclaim it.

I am in the audience in a large auditorium, like a school performance. Love song after love song after love song. We lip-sync along, we cry and cry. I am in a dance on the beach with Thrivers. We pull each other in and out of the water. Sharla speaks, her shirt coming undone. Cait is there, she is with the baby, she has been offered a new place to live. AD is there - she is kind, she's brainstorming new places for Cait but it is the students that come through. Houses on Lee & Mayfield houses on Lee & Van Aken. We can't walk home together even though we want to because we are going two different directions.

I am in high school and find a way to sign myself out for the day, so Vilde and I can take a road-trip. I feel awkward, freshly liberated, breaking the rules to be walking out of the school building and getting into this funny little car he has. The steering is (typically) in the back seat, pedals way low, steering also low: a small black disc. I sit between his legs to steer, but that doesn't really work either. // The park at South Park: I am walking through the woods, a group of teens is gathering behind me, near Shaker blvd. One of the girls runs up to me, tries to try to take my purse. Not suave. We talk. She admits to recent sex, random, for fun, forgetting she might be fertile. I walk into her house. It is full of massage tables. I engage in conversation about receiving one and it is non conclusive. I am only told the practitioner in this house is well known.

I live at the airport, on standby to leave. The power goes out. Confusion, chaos. And yet, trust that all will be well. I return 'home' to the dark glass doors and windows and am surprised by how it looks desolate, deserted, dangerous. When cars go by, past the empty parking lot, I try to wave them down and am ignored. Judy Evans shows up to run a group. I ask to help her with carrying a few things, she says she is fine without but I want to, to speak to her. I tell her the situation and she opens her home to me.

My lover is on a test to not love me physically. We are on a 'date' we are in a bed, our legs entwine but the energy is contracted, guilty, confused. I argue for just letting go & melting into it. Please kiss this skin! A dog wanders around. We debate. The energy sways another way than our bodies but I trust that all is well.

Art exhibition - blender: 2big names in expo together. Abramowicz in response to that man who does huge white canvas. We sit in circle to admire in view and in discussion. // the house with the muddy path winding out, off the back door. I take a bike to explore; I follow it like a giddy kid. I tell friends what a treat to have found this place, we gather in joy.

I am outside with a crowd of people, much like the courtyard of the school in Bures-sur-Yvette. The waiting classroom, present in the corner. We are freezing the temperature has changed to cold. Perhaps snow. I wrap myself in my yak and face it relatively well.

Looking through binoculars, I see the caves in the side of the mountain, right outside of the window. There is also a giant Shiva statue. I have been jogging in white as part of a routine- how I get to where I am going, or at least a ritual I take part in. Jeremy is with me. We are then in a classroom. There are over 20 of us. It will be clay or paper mâché. Stations are limited and the priority is made by enthusiasm and attendance. I know I'll be first if that's the criteria. We move into a side room, sit along a table. Even though I know that I am 'first' - I get stuck on a chair in the corner. Tough access to the table. There is a hallway off of the classroom with museum displays: glass panels protect vases and Asian artifacts. The light is yellow.

I am at a Thrive event. Gold backdrops and microphones. I am in the pit, Uma and friends are setting up to perform music. Improv, invented instrument music. When they are ready to begin, I need to climb up on the stage to be an observer, an audience member. The group of 6 or 7 spaced out like folks comfortably in a living room make percussion with drumsticks and clapping. Something about the dress that I am wearing and managing my hair, slightly different. Peeling out of the layer. Feeling powerful and yet nervous. Gold.

I'm on a train pulling into station. I have a transfer. Something about Moscow. My bags need to be claimed. There are hundreds of them in the corridor. Luckily mine have a distinct color and after some hesitation, some panic, I get all of my pieces and begin to figure out which platform we are on and which one I need to be on.

I am at a huge meditation/yoga event. I trade in my wooden Mala for a citrine one. The weight of stones around my neck, I stand taller. I am with logistics. Half participating, half on the computer. I draw boxes in ASCII. Persian carpets, we sit in lines and squares.

On a long train journey, maybe days, I am Cautious about the last few stops. Consider sleeping but fear missing my station. I am in a house-sized bedroom and I check the hour. I have 50 minutes. Staszek said something about if he were still living in his old place, he could take another stop and that registered so hard, I keep checking which stop that is and keep reminding myself that he will not expect to go down there, as it is no longer his place. We are in a gym to dance some form of contra dance, some form of square. We configure and reconfigure, switch from east-west lines to north-south, shuffle partners. I am invited to join a woman who says, specifically, that she can be touched by the person who I am partnered with. I am organizing cleaning supplies in small cups: a sponge, rubber gloves. I consolidate to make room for more.

I meet with friends in a diner and we smoke pot. I am self-conscious about the smoke, the scent, so I inhale immensely - the cigarette-joint crackles as I draw in 1/3 of its length. It is daytime and there is a light wood color. A few tables over the the group that I am part of. There is a participant who is only staying for part of the event. He is on the phone with the leader of the workshop, sweet-talking, saying he is going to send everyone he knows to take part -even though he himself is leaving early.

I am in Thrive training. Jesse asks a question that I have the answer to. I run over the bridge and grab a shiny coat hanger to prove that. The group is small, I feel like I stand a chance to be seen and share my gifts. I wave the hanger. I am recognized.

Chaotic room, strangers milling around. Late into the evening. The main resident is moving. We help gather a few things together. I stack a few candy dishes and throw in small objects: a lighter, a book of matches, little tchotchkes. Comforting this mover that all will be done, safely and fast. She said, don't worry about it. We are working quickly and behind the uncle's back. // Eleanor the Mercedes, driving in a city then country. Maybe New York or DC. Tree-shaded boulevard yields into wide highway in the fog.

I am on my hands and knees scrubbing the floor in the big room at Boboli. I scrape up every board individually. Clumps of gray gook come up. I wonder if I will have to then refinish or at least wax the floors since they are coming up worn. Margot walks in with Martina. Dramatic and stately. She sits down, I can feel us both expecting a significant reaction. I do not budge from my work beyond a hello. I tell her that I must finish this work. I avoid eye contact. I fear the moment when I'll have to actually interact.

1: party? I need to leave and am parked in by Gabriela in a white stick-shift. She is in her mode of innocence. I get the keys and move the car as if on a monitor. 2: Vilde has reset the alarm, a little later. Beautiful music, like dead can dance wake us up but I panic. The clock says 6:45 or is it :15 maybe :75 The numbers keep switching. I am sweaty and confused. There are 3 of us. I go to shower and our other lover aims to get Vilde in the shower, too. I think about going out with wet hair and whether that is dangerous before I travel. I sit on the toilet and pee for long minutes.

Lorka lives somewhere exotic. Maybe even china. Or India. I visit and play with clothing for a video shoot. I have ideas and suggestions, getting the director's attention to give opinions about color and shimmy. We leave and as we walk towards The car, there is a shady man getting into the car next to ours. I ask That we slow down, really slow down to give him time to move out and away. We actually walk around the block. It is night time, the buildings are dark, industrially dirty. Around the corner, Dee is sitting near her car, speaking to cops in their car. We make passerby comments and continue. Driving off, we go through tunnels and under bridges. Then in a large open intersection, near park/woods.

Standing at a sink, doing dishes. I sing Peter Gabriel's In Your Eyes, then play it from some electronic device. The kitchen is not mine, I have lived here temporarily and am in the process of leaving. I make small piles of precious objects, like earrings made from handmade paper- on the counter then on the stairs. There are two others in they kitchen with me: a man and a woman. They are siblings. They are impressed with the things I find and at the way I am able to organize the objects in the dishwasher. Large white cutting boards. There is another song, about romance. About a woman asking a man if he is too warm and taking off her shirt to break the ice. I imagine the song to take place near a pond, summer weather of course.

Walking down an industrial setting, the male workers and others are sleazy - they ask me my name, they ask me my age, they don't ask permission to touch. One grabs my shoulders so I turn around to defend myself. I have no physical fighting skills. His leg is up after a kick to my crotch; I grab it and am unable to knock him over as I hoped to do. // a long string of wire, first I untangle like earphone cable. Then, the two younger boys have it and I help them finish it decoratively. I twist and then undo and redo because there are six strands not 4. I realize I can divide into three - n - three by color rather than keep them in their original mixed pairs.

Scouting for a schooling location, moving from loft apt outside and back. We go to the wood nearby, recommended. I worry about trash and sure enough, as we drive in, we see a huge, home entertainment wide screen TV - on and playing. Back in the loft, the bathrooms are like those in airplanes, sliding accordion doors and minimalist spacing.

I am about to teach a class on posture and postural analysis, on healthy body mechanics. My students are gathering in the building, a dark brown barn structure past the atrium/greenhouse space of the main bldg. I decide to get some icecream. I pay $6.50 and wait. And wait. And wait. The cashier is not moving towards making my ice cream. Martina says she'll have done if I get part chocolate. I ask if they can do swirl. He says no. I ask if half vanilla half chocolate is an option - he says no. I am frustrated and running late to teach. My props are falling out of my hands: books and notebooks, my grandmother's tennis shoe, to show the wear on the sole. Finally I ask for my money back and leave, ice-cream free.

Adult school: massage and/or yoga. Carpet and fabrics. Crowds walking around, entering the back space through the back door but it is only an alternate passageway to the other room. Views and nature, walking in snow. My companion is a mix of Michael & Vilde, maybe dreadlocks, too. I am excited to be in his company. // I am sitting at the top of some red carpeted stairs. I have a beverage of some sort, which I spill in simulation of orgasm. I find this to be an important task or test: to lessen the shock of my puddle-making, to demonstrate powerful orgasm, to check how easy it is to clean up.

I am in a kitchen with a large number of women. We are talking and animated. I am given soup in a bowl the size of a bottle cap and I request to have it served inside of an open drawer. This causes some grumpiness, some dissatisfaction. We react to news shared, to concepts. Eating is the matrix our lives develop in.

I live on a shady block. My townhouse has pillars and dealers killing around. I walk home at night with my heart pounding in fear, I pass 2 men (at some distance from each other) who are working the curb with their rocks of crack. I slip into the door and move through the motions: locking the door, turning on the light, getting off coat.

I am on the phone with Laura Cyrocki. We talk about her emotional ins and outs and I tell her that there have been times when I have not felt her, felt disconnected - that there have been times when I have felt her energetically drop out. // I am on a first floor balcony/deck covered with snow. It is a celebration like New Years. There are fireworks and other light show elements. The fireworks explode in the sky and they blossom on the ground. They spell words and offer entire sentences. We realize that the neighbor from upstairs has peed down on the deck and soiled our perfect snow. // turning the car around in the garage. I am fearful, apprehensive. The driver does fine and slips out perfectly.

I ride my bicycle home after some sort of trouble. I lock it up in the Boboli parking lot. When I come back, it is gone. I am confused and appalled. I look for it as if I might have put it elsewhere. But it is gone. The somewhere where I had stepped out to was a gathering with a psychic, a channel, like Esther Hicks. We had moments up close and then we had crowds. I was trying to take photos, then help a short friend see by holding her up, over the other heads. // I am in a strange large kitchen in the process of being taken apart. A team of movers talks about how they will take the pieces out. The woman who is leaving is packing and nervous and not remembering how these pieces were brought in, in the first place, which elicits reactions from the movers.

I am in a giant aquarium. There is a small whale there. There are also a number of smaller aquariums in the huge one, I wonder about this separation and what one must do to clean them. We bring in a second large fish, a shark. I worry about the interactions of these two, as I observe them from the inside of the pond- breathing freely in the water- but they seem fine.

I am the passenger on a small flight machine. It is open and vulnerable. The black seat, a slick leather piece like a drum kit stool- there are no seat belts or other straps. My driver, a mechanical guy, is telling me a story. I twist around to interact and feel the precariousness of my perch. We are not very high, just a few stories above the gravel lot where this thing operates. I mention the danger. He confirms, to be careful. I turn around again to comment and slip right off of the seat. I am clinging on with my arms, surprised at the sense of strength I find there, yet aware of the peril. We move towards the ground. I feel gawker eyes on me. Ultimately, I am safe.

Martina and Margo are pregnant and giving birth on the same day. We are in fancy hotels, ski lodges, the bath tubs are wide and deep. I want to help, but feel in the way. I want to witness, but feel uninvited. I want to celebrate, but carry a sense of failure here: no relationship, no baby. Inadequacy in where I've come. Martina is in another building and I hear news of her successful birth. I won't even go see her until tomorrow, even though she is just a few steps away. I remember the other dream, where she was wearing a baby and seemed like such a natural, such a pro - I think, in the dream, that that dream was prophetic.

I am in a red and white elevator that does not stop on the 24th floor, where we want to go - it just keeps going. The floor selection keypad is a wild remote-controlled programming unit. it takes longer to program it than for the lift to cross floors. We go further up, try to stop it on the way down, are heading towards the ground floor, seems like too much time and too much up and down. // I am in a hostel/room-for-rent situation. A bedroom with 3 beds magically unfolds into 6 beds, when what seemed like a wall opens. Several very 'adult' people are looking at it. African-American women, in glasses.

I walk into the water, the waves crash small, manageably, and their push of riding out to the shore is a strong currant which surfs my body. I am walking out on my knees because of the shallows. My clothing, a tank top, is riding up in the water. My companion, a stranger, encourages this drift, hints to remove the clothing all together. // I am in a clothing store, looking at tank tops. All black, and turquoise with black and all turquoise. I am also being guided and approved of by a benevolent stranger.

Atmarupa and I speak briefly: attendance has been better. A couple connected to the center is there. They were just on a road trip to South Point. For the second time. She doesn't acknowledge the first because she was fresh off of international travel and slept the whole way. A woman of Donna Mazola's stature learns to 3-point turn a Haflinger. She downplays the effort, wants to leave the vehicle in the courtyard, we remind her the travels begin. Shortly, at a stoplight, we must break ice gathered at the front wheels, shovel it to the back, this gives us traction and we're able to go effortlessly.

A cluster of pumpkin balloons plays outside the window of Boboli. There is also a cluster inside. Helium, they bob and dance in the different ceiling heights. We are several and it has gotten steamy (literally). We are waiting. Waiting for the show, for the call from the driver to fine-tune the logistics, coming to get us after dropping off the director. There is a lot of love among us. In the theater, I sit by the aisle. The show has begun but the crew is still setting up the next, carrying huge signage down the house, resting it right by my seat, cautioning us that it is freshly painted.

On a train for just 2 maybe 3 stops- urban stations, names I didn't recognize, route established by my grandmother who I imagined found the shortest walk to where we were going. Art. A small round swimming pool. The sky, textured of the moon. Swimming circles in white - maybe not water.

Swimming pool, most of the people are naked. I am in suit, coordinating with a group of dancers. Sweater, backpack. They are leaving today and only 2 will stay. They move into refurbished rooms. The rest descend a long and wide staircase to the street below. The crowd is young, my colleague has arranged half of a gym to play basketball. I smell smoke, twice, associate it with D. & awake. I am frantically planning the expansion/ arrangement of Gzowo, believing myself to be in the US, but Lorka thanks me for thinking of Poland first. The woods are tall and still.

He's on his first week of driving the new train, the one suspended from above like in Wuppertal. I am privy to sit up front and he is amazed to get the right of way in the towns, giddy like a child- he's spent his career preparing for this. Laura Cyrocki and I are sitting after school, she is having trouble motivating herself to go home. We are on benches in a darkened hallway. I offer support in moving the mind. Turns out it was about food and we set off together to eat at the local restaurant. She wants pizza with meat. We cross the street and then walk through a shallow creek bed towards the high-sitting restaurant, with the giant neon across its facade.

Somehow at camp. A table lined with us eating our meals. The vegetarian question of course central. I have ham on my plate which I diligently pack into a small plastic bag and think, for the cat. The bus comes to collect half of us. Two buses, right in there among the tables, filled with people, I am sitting between them, on the floor, feeling important. I move out of their way and go to finish my food, the rest of my group, the remaining group is taken with playing pickup sticks. I eat and help cleanup go in to play. My set is smaller- thinner, less bulky and my toothbrush is full of sand... Or salt... I go to wash it. Iza is there doing laundry. Cussing about her dislike of laundry. Saying she'd rather just buy new clothes than hand wash jeans. I am washing a large pair of underware. She comments. Everything I have is sea green.

In a makeshift theater, the stage a diorama in a cardboard box, we watch Busia's art masterpiece. I drive in snow, nearly slipping into the drivers in front of me. I take unknown turns and end in dead end cul de sacs, strange women kindly offer me direction out. I have my own cup of tea, and want to sit in the coffee shop I made it to, respite, decide to buy cake to pay for the seat and I am distracted by the high-lit white bathrooms and more advice from women.

Relocating to the forest, to being with a community of highly technological processes in the setting of trees. I am moving from a 2 room apartment that I share with a lesbian couple. They are reading all of my books, since I am about to pack them. The larger one has on a sweatshirt made of a cloth that takes on different colors by angle of light. A velour shag of orange on a purple base. I am massaging a helium balloon, because it feels good. The air is going down. I decide to cut it, inhale and I speak like an elf much to the delight of these 2 women. I am cooking a potato that is falling apart- toasty on the edge. I add left-over potato from another dish, now cold, to warm up along with this freshly made one and I turn off the heat.

I am sitting at a table with a lover who might not yet be my lover, who, like me has travel plans, might be gone soon, yet we discovered that our departures aren't for another week or so. I plan to spend them as close to him as I manage. We sit down at that restaurant, dark lighting, the one that leads to that room with a giant pool. I have to use the bathroom and when I go- finishing a squat toi-toi, my body produces endless poop. First shaped and solid then just cream excretion, endless, happening below me and without my effort. It piles so high in the toilet bowl that my genitals a soiled. I find a laundry basket in arms reach and use a pink sweater and an old towel to clean myself up. Then I return to my table nonchalantly.

We are in a house, maybe K-house, Laura Cyrocki and an unknown woman. I am learning to navigate a new set of friends, of responsibility. Cats get out into the snow. I am looking through a bin of clothing, soft pinks, designer labels. The clothes will soon all be catalogued in a world-wide database of outfits. We'll be able to create combinations with easy clicks. I am excited and overwhelmed. We gather with others, in a room with an orange couch. The leader knows us well, she tells us where and how to sit. // I am driving in the rain at night and it takes me several attempts to get the windshield wipers fast enough. // glass elevator, bank of 4 escalators, all coming down when I want to go up. The one that is going up has an elder gentleman coming down on it. The shopping center is closing but I am determined to get there. So much so, I am walking a good 10 yards ahead of my friends.

I am in the kitchen with Mantram and another woman. She hands me a neti pot to use but there is old food caked to the bottom: peas and carrots. As I look at it more deliberately, I realize it is cleanable so I let it soak and then scrape with a fork. In the meantime, I talk to the others about YS1, or is it a special workshop? A special training? I have a bonus set of material from a psychic, available for download. // Dancing in the rain. Swirling in various intensities of downpour. Like camping and I am totally prepared.

I am running on an orange rubber track, it goes around a large room, a small park. I follow purple & green tags, like on yoga mats, that say 'books'. Swami Atmarupa shows up with a clip board. For a moment I am self-conscious for running but then I think that the short distance is different. And I am in great shape, stamina is high. I was running with another woman, passing others. I ask Atmarupa where to buy something and it turns out to be nearby. I make a plan to loop through this mall, and severance. Crossing the street. Snow.

I am driving in slipper snow down winding country roads. I miss a curve in the road and drive into a field. I just make a loop in the snow to catch the road again. I hope that turning onto a main road will be safer, but that road is not plowed. I fear for the brakes. I pass a medieval tower with Arabic writing. I know this is a landmark for where I am going. I take a turn and the car drives into a dead end cafe courtyard. I turn around and am now walking. I walk to the main road and the car is parked right there, running. I get in he passenger side door and skootch over to drive but realize that I am in the back seat. I get out and back into the passenger front door to again move into the driver seat and sort through my directions to figure out where I need to go. I feel lost in the unknown.

Heat: in the kitchen at K-house, I open all the windows and find windows in places unexpected. I am sad, maybe I've been crying, a vulnerable edge... I go to the Thrive Speaker training. I am impressed at myself for having made it to California. The crowd is on the small side, somewhat lackluster, dwindling. I talk on the phone during the presentation. Feeling sort of bad about it. I thought I was using the sink to wash my hands, but the turn of the left handle called a group of assassins to my house. My entire family was massacred, but I didn't see because I was in another room. I cornered one of the assassins, ready to kill him, when some others snuck up behind to kill me.

Allison and i ride on horseback over to a seemingly normal village a mile away. Upon hitting the end of the village she turns around and by the stables pushes me off, telling me to steal a horse.
